info.title: Madar API
info.description: Madar POS — multi-tenant cafe and restaurant management. The Rust backend is the source of truth for this spec; the Flutter teller app and React management dashboard consume the generated openapi.json.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.description:
When set, prices are branch-effective (override replaces default_price) and
addons disabled at this branch are excluded — the per-branch addon list the
POS consumes. Omitted → the plain org list (legacy behaviour).

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive filter on the addon name.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
Sending `page` or `per_page` switches the response to the paginated
shape (`PaginatedAddonItems`); without either it stays the plain array
the POS and old clients read.

200.description: List addon items. A plain array; with `page` or `per_page` the paginated `PaginatedAddonItems` shape.

post.summary:
A fresh staff token for the phone that sends its device token in
`X-Staff-Device` (RO-3). The device is the refresh credential: once it is
revoked (a new phone, a new number, the employee deactivated) this answers
401 `DEVICE_REVOKED` and the app signs out. The same checks as every
`/staff/*` call: the employee is active with app access, the business is
active and has Dawam on.

parameters.description:
Include flags already reviewed. Default false: the queue is what is left
to look at.

parameters.name: approval
parameters.description:
Optional one-time manager approval, the ordinary `ReplayApproval` shape
JSON-encoded (a GET has no body). A till signed in as a TELLER uses it
to pull its own branch's flags with a manager's PIN; leaving it out is
exactly the old behaviour, `approvals.review` on the bearer.

post.summary:
Resolve many flags at once — "select many" or "everything for this till or
day" from the dashboard's review queue (owner, 2026-09-17). Extends
[`review_flag`] rather than duplicating it: same capability, same
semantics (an acknowledgement, not an approval), now with an optional note
and one id at a time so a bad id among many never loses the rest.

`seated` → `completed` by hand. The party is done with the booking; if
they never started a bill under it, the hold seating placed is let go of
too (a bill, had there been one, would have ended it `seated` already and
its settle buses the table). Already `completed` is a clean 200.

get.summary:
The counter's join QR: a static, per-branch card that opens the public
signup form. Static on purpose — it is printed once and stood on a counter,
so it must keep working with no reprint. The per-CUSTOMER QR is a different
thing entirely: it lives on their Wallet pass and carries their member token.

get.summary:
Suggest menu items frequently ordered alongside the given item set, to help
a manager pick the next component while building a bundle. Anchors on
whichever items are already added: an item is suggested if it co-occurred,
on the same order, with at least one anchor item at least `min_count`
times across the org's branches in the given window.

parameters.name: item_ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated menu item IDs already added to the in-progress bundle.

parameters.name: min_count
parameters.description:
Minimum number of orders an item must co-occur with the anchor set in
to be suggested. Default 3.

post.summary: Mark a bussed table ready for the next party.
post.description:
The ONE human act the ledger cannot derive. Everything else about a
table's status follows from its rows: seated while one is live, dirty
after a checkout ended it. But no server can see that the plates have been
cleared, so a person says so, and the row records who.

Deliberately not a set-status endpoint. Its predecessor took any status and
wrote it with no lock and no occupancy check, so it could declare a table
free while a ticket was open on it. This performs exactly one transition,
`dirty` -> `free`, and refuses anything else.

get.summary: A table's history and what it earns.
get.description:
The link was always there and nothing ever read it: a settled bill carries
`orders.open_ticket_id`, and the ticket carries `table_id`. So a table's
takings are one join away, and until now a shop could see a room full of
tables and not answer "which of these actually earns".

Covers and money count SETTLED bills only. An open bill is still running
and a voided one took nothing — folding either into the averages would
flatter a table that lost money.

post.summary: Take a table for a party with no bill yet.
post.description:
Occupancy travels on its own here, carrying nothing about what is on the
table -- but always who took it: the hold is a `party` row in the ledger
owned by the hand that placed it, so there is no such thing as a table held
by nobody. Two things use it:

  * A PARTY SITTING DOWN. They have ordered nothing yet, so there is no
    bill — a ticket starts with their first round and claims this table on
    the way in. Seating used to open an empty ticket instead, which put a
    zero-value bill in every report and made a party who changed their mind
    and left something you had to VOID.
  * A PARKED CART. Device-local by design: the order, its lines and its
    money never leave the till. But the table is not the till's private
    business, and while it stayed local the dashboard's floor and every
    other terminal were told a table with somebody's order waiting on it was
    free.

In both cases the server learns that the table is taken, by whom and from
which till, and nothing whatever about what is on it.

Like `clear_table`, and for the reason written there, this is not a
set-status endpoint: exactly one transition, `free` -> `seated`, refused
from anything else with a `code` the till can act on. A table a ticket is
already on stays the ticket's; a table another till holds stays theirs.

post.summary: Give back a table a till was holding for its own parked order.
post.description:
The counterpart to `hold_table`: the hold moved to another table, was
checked out, or was discarded. Ends the `party` row -- leaving the table
`free`, or `dirty` when `bus` says the party ate -- and never touches a
ticket's: if one has landed since, the ticket owns the table and this is a
no-op rather than a way to free an occupied table.

Not owner-gated on purpose. The draft is device-local and outlives a shift
handover, so the teller who checks it out is often not the one who parked
it; the ledger records who released it instead of refusing them.

This used to FORGET the person — it was written when the loyalty row was the
only record of them. A membership is now a card under the customer's id, so
ending it touches nothing but the card: the customer, their orders, their
addresses and their bookings stay, and they can join again. Erasing a
person's data is `POST /customers/{id}/erase`, which also ends the card.
See [`model::leave`] for exactly what goes.

204 twice in a row: a card that is already gone is not a failure.

get.summary: What Google is actually holding for one member's card. **Super admin only.**
get.description:
The nearby-notification question has been answered three times by reasoning
and never by looking: either the `locations` are on the object Google holds
and the gap is in what Google does with them, or they never arrived and the
gap is ours. Both stories fit every symptom from the outside; only the object
separates them. This returns it verbatim, unsummarised, because a summary
would be one more layer of my guessing between the evidence and the reader.

Super admin for the same reason as `wallet_status`: it is Madar's plumbing,
named in Google's vocabulary, and there is nothing an org manager could do
with it.

post.summary:
Provision this member's Google card and report every word of it.
**Super admin only.**
post.description:
Reading the object back says what Google HOLDS. It does not say why, and by
the time you are reading it the write that mattered is over — a refused
class refresh is deliberately only a warning, because a customer must keep
the card they have, so the reason goes to a log rather than to the person
asking the question.

This runs the real provisioning through the real code path, keeping a
transcript: every request, its status, and Google's answer verbatim. Then it
reads both resources back, so the transcript and the outcome sit together.

It WRITES, which is why it is a POST and why it is not part of any page
load. Everything it does, opening a customer's card page does too.

get.summary: Why there is no "Add to Wallet" button. **Super admin only.**
get.description:
Every failure in this feature has looked the same from the outside — a
missing button, or a save that says "something went wrong" — while the cause
was a variable nobody set, a key file the code never read, a service account
Google had not been told about, or a link over a size limit. None of those
reach a customer's screen, and only some reach a log.

This asks, on demand, and reports what it finds. It makes live calls to
Google, so it is deliberately not part of any page load.

get.summary: The member's own purchase history.
get.description:
Authenticated by the token in the URL — the same one their pass carries and
the till scans — because that is the only credential a loyalty member has.
Which means anyone holding the link can read it, and that is worth stating
rather than glossing: a forwarded card link forwards the history with it.
The shop decides whether to run a programme on those terms, and the privacy
policy says so plainly.

Voided orders are excluded. A sale that was reversed is not something the
customer bought, and showing it invites a question the page cannot answer.

get.summary: The shop's own logo, as a favicon.
get.description:
Square, opaque, and on the shop's own ground — the same treatment the
wallet badge gets, and for the same reason: a browser tab and an iOS home
screen both draw this against a background they choose, so a mark on
transparency is a coin flip and a wide wordmark cropped to a square loses
the shop's name. [`crate::orgs::branding::on_ground`] fits the artwork
whole and centres it, which is why a wordmark reads as a band rather than
as two letters.

The inset is wider than the wallet's. Nothing masks a favicon to a circle,
so there is no reason to leave the corners empty.

A shop with no logo gets a 404, and the page falls back to whatever icon it
shipped with — Madar's. That is the honest answer: this endpoint serves a
shop's logo, and there isn't one.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description:
Rounded up to 32, 180 or 512. Defaults to 180 — big enough for a home
screen, and a browser downsamples for the tab perfectly well.

mode.description:
"auto" | "open" | "closed". Named `mode` (not `override`) because a bare
`override` field is a reserved word in Dart and breaks the POS client
code generator.

device_code.description:
The device's short code on receipts (`T1`); a default is derived when
absent or invalid.

device_token.description:
The device's own credential. Returned ONCE; store it in the device
vault. Sent later as `X-Madar-Device-Token`.

code.description: The 8 digits. Shown while free; kept afterwards so the list reads.

AddonCost.description: Computed cost for one addon item.

cost.description:
Ingredient cost rollup in piastres over the ingredients that *are*
priced. A partial rollup still returns the sum so far, with
`cost_missing = true`; `null` only when nothing is priced.

cost_missing.description:
`true` when at least one ingredient is unlinked or has no cost, so `cost`
(if any) is partial rather than the full figure.

margin_pct.description: `(price - cost) / price` — only when the cost is *complete* and price > 0.

unit_price.description:
Charged unit price (piastres) the POS applied for this addon. When present
it is RECORDED as the addon's unit_price; absent → the server's expected
(catalog) price is used. Bundle-component addons ignore this (server-priced).

pricing.description:
How a sale line charges this option: madar-catalog's `OptionView`
(branch-effective price, its group's effect and swap category, the
ingredient it replaces, its lines per size). The till prices lines with
it exactly as the order path does. Additive; older tills ignore it.

category_id.description:
The ingredient's category (additive, B12): lets the POS know an extra
shot is a `coffee_bean` and follows the drink's chosen bean.

decided_by.description:
Who decided a line that waited for the owner, when, and why (a
rejection always says why, D8).

effective_date.description: The month it lands in (the first day of a recurring line, AD-1/AD-3).

reason_code.description:
A rule-made line's reason as a code and its figures (`late`
`{minutes}`, `absent_no_punch`, …), the payslip breakdown's own, so a
client words it in its language (AT-13, E2E B-PAY-4). Null for a
bonus and for a manual line (its `reason` is what was typed).

value_piastres.description:
A percent line valued against the salary, in piastres — the server's
figure (AT-3); equals `amount_piastres` for a flat line.

waived_at.description: A rule-made deduction the manager forgave: shown, counted for nothing (AD-6/AD-8).

expense.description: Cash for shop purchases: a log, never deducted (AV-7).

oneOf.description: A finding, with the data behind it.
One question back before the assistant can proceed.
It could not get to an answer. Any data it did gather is still returned.

AiChatKind.description: How the turn ended. Every variant is a 200.

conversation_id.description:
Continue a stored conversation. When set, history is loaded from the
server and `history` below is ignored — this is the path that gives
resumable chats and unlimited, compacted context.

Omit it to start a new conversation; the response says which one was
created.

history.description:
Recent prior turns, oldest first. The stateless fallback, kept for
clients that manage their own window and for one-off questions. Ignored
when `conversation_id` is set. The server caps it regardless.

locale.description:
Answer language — "en" or "ar" (default "en"). Drives translated labels
and the reply language.

question.description:
The merchant's plain-language question, e.g. "top 5 products last month"
or "أعلى ٥ منتجات الشهر الماضي".

conversation_id.description:
The conversation this turn belongs to. Present whenever the turn was
stored — send it back on the next message to continue.

timezone.description: The timezone every date in the answer is expressed in.

AnalyticsOrder.description: One order, reduced to the money that belongs to the order itself.

order_number.description: Per-shift sequence number shown on the POS.

order_ref.description:
The human-readable reference printed on the receipt
(`<BRANCHCODE>-<YYMMDD>-<NNNN>`). Null for orders predating it.

service_charge.description:
The service charge added to this order, `0` where the branch charges
none. This was a hard-coded `0` for every order — the field was
published as if it meant something while a service charge did not
exist. It does now, and this is it.

subtotal.description: Piastres. Sum of the line items before discount and tax.

total_amount.description:
`subtotal - discount_amount + service_charge + tax_amount`. Deliberately COMPUTED rather
than read from `orders.total_amount`, which also carries the delivery
fee — this figure is the order's own value and nothing else. Tips are
excluded too (they are not part of `total_amount` in the first place).

avg_order_total.description:
`total_revenue / total_orders`, truncated to whole piastres. 0 when the
window is empty.

from_utc.description:
The exact half-open instant window `[from_utc, to_utc)` the figures
cover, echoed so there is never a question about what was included.

limit.description: Echo of the paging actually applied, and how many rows came back.

timezone.description: IANA zone the business days were resolved in.

total_orders.description:
Orders in the window. Voided and refunded orders are excluded here and
everywhere below, as are orders tendered with a payment method the
merchant has hidden from partners — none are returned at all.

sizes_changed.description: Sizes (incl. linked copies) whose stored lines changed.

sizes_seen.description: Sizes examined (every size of every live item in the org).

sizes_with_manual_packaging.description:
Sizes that still have an OWN line in a packaging category: typed by hand, they
are kept (and win over a rule for the same ingredient) — review them.

sizes_with_rule.description: Sizes that now carry at least one rule line.

my_date.description: The date of MY shift I give away.

my_shift_id.description: MY shift (a block I'm rostered on that date).

peer_date.description: The date of the colleague's shift I take.

suggested_deduction_piastres.description: Time away × the person's minute rate, rounded to the nearest 5 EGP (CL-7).

check_out_reason.description:
Why someone else punched this person OUT; the in-reason stays in
`punch_reason` (AT-10, Mac E2E BC-1).

covered_employee_id.description: A cover: whose shift this person worked (CV-*).

month_closed.description:
Its day is in an approved or paid month (period_lock): an overtime or
cover approval, a correction or a deduction on it is refused with
PERIOD_CLOSED, so clients don't offer them.

punch_reason.description: Why someone else punched this person IN (or the only punch they made).

status_overridden.description: A manager set this day's status by hand; automation keeps it (AT-7).

advance_cap_percent.description: Salary advances owed may reach this share of monthly salary (AV-5).

cover_pay_mode.description:
How a confirmed cover is paid (owner decision D5): `minute_rate` (the
coverer's day rate ÷ 8 h × the minutes covered, CV-4; the default) or
`full_block` (the covered block as a full day). A branch may override
it (listed in `overridden`).

excused_time_paid_default.description:
Whether an approved mid-shift permission or early departure is PAID by
default. The approver may override it on any individual request.

gender_mode.description: `off` · `soft` · `hard`: how the gender default weighs in suggestions (SC-12).

half_day_leave_counts.description: `half_shift` · `whole_day`: what a half-day leave counts as (RQ-8).

holiday_multiplier.description: What working a set-up holiday pays (RU-10).

limit_day_hours.description:
Labour limits, hours (RU-13). They warn, never block, and stay
unconfirmed until a lawyer signs them off.

night_start.description: Night for the night overtime rate and for suggestions (RU-8, RU-9).

orders_per_staff.description: POS-derived coverage: one person per this many orders an hour.

overridden.description:
For a branch: the rules it sets itself (every other field is the
business's, RU-2). Empty for the business.

period_start_day.description: Day of the month a pay period opens (PAY-1): 26 = a 26th–25th cycle.

rules_saved_at.description: When the business saved its rules; nobody clocks in before (RU-1).

suggested_tiers.description: The ladder the set-up step suggests (RU-1). Never used for pricing.

AttendanceStatus.description:
The five mutually-exclusive states an attendance row can be in.

Stored as `text` with a CHECK constraint rather than a Postgres enum: statuses
here are a closed set we control, and text avoids the `ALTER TYPE ... ADD
VALUE` transaction dance every time the set grows.

AttendanceSummary.description: One employee's totals over a reporting window.

code.description:
A stable code for a label the SERVER wrote (`unspecified`,
`correction_request`, `auto_closed`, a void reason), so a client
words it in its own language (AT-13, E2E B-PAY-5). Absent for a
person's own words (a typed reason, a name): `label` is the text.

by_kind.description:
Discounts audit only: by act (`preset` / `manual_amount` /
`manual_percent`; `unattributed` for sales from before). Additive.

entries.description:
Discounts audit only: the most recent discounted sales, newest first
(at most 200). Additive.

history.description:
Deduction overrides audit only: every waive, unwaive and override
event with who, when and why, newest first (at most 500) — the
history, so a waiver later undone still shows (owner decision D8,
AT-10). Additive.

AuthzPublicKey.description: A public key a device verifies snapshots with.

order_id.description: The server's order id — the history path, where the order is synced.

order_key.description:
The client-minted idempotency key — the just-checked-out path, where the
order may not have reached the server yet. Resolved to the same order.

requested_at.description:
When the teller pressed the button. Absent = now.

An offline till stamps the press and queues it, so a drain days later
still credits an award that was made in time. Bounded on arrival (see
the module docs) so it cannot be used to reach outside the window.

token.description: Who. A scanned pass token, a typed phone, or an already-resolved member.

already_awarded.description:
True when this order had already earned — a double tap, a retry, or a
replayed offline op. Not an error: the outcome is the one that was asked
for, and the response carries the balance that resulted.

points_awarded.description: Points this sale earned. 0 when it was too small to reach one point.

BirthdayPreview.description: The birthday greeting as it would actually be sent, in both languages.

auto_no_show_minutes.description:
Unseated this long after `starts_at` → `no_show` automatically. `null`
= only when the window ends.

blackout_dates.description: ISO dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`) with no online slots.

enabled.description: Online (public) booking switch. Host bookings work regardless.

hold_minutes.description: The floor shows the table as held from `starts_at - hold_minutes`.

max_covers_per_slot.description: Optional ceiling on guests whose bookings start in one slot.

require_otp.description: Online guests must verify their phone by WhatsApp code.

covers.description: Guests across bookings that were seated or completed.

no_show_rate.description: no_show / (no_show + seated + completed), 0 when nothing happened.

customer_id.description:
The customer who booked (design §2.5); `guest_name` / `guest_phone`
beside it are the snapshot of what was typed. `None` for a booking
from before customers existed whose phone is not a valid number.

held_from.description:
The floor shows the claimed tables as held from here (branch
`hold_minutes` before the start). Clients compare with their clock.

needs_table.description: Active but holding no table: the host must assign one.

open_ticket_id.description:
The ticket this party is (or was) eating on. DERIVED from
`open_tickets.booking_id` — the live one if there is one, else the
latest — never stored on the booking.

code.description:
Short org-unique branch prefix (A-Z0-9) embedded in every order_ref
(`<CODE>-YYMMDD-…`). Exposed so an offline device can mint the same ref the
server would, from first boot, without waiting for a synced order.

geo_radius_meters.description: Radius in meters within which this branch is considered a match. Defaults to 200.

latitude.description: WGS-84 latitude for geofenced branch resolution.

longitude.description: WGS-84 longitude for geofenced branch resolution.

old_bill_hours.description:
A bill left open longer than this many hours is flagged as OLD (till
open notice, close warning, Z report). 1..168, default 3.

org_logo_url.description: Convenience field — populated from the parent org's `logo_url`.

org_receipt_footer.description:
Convenience field — the parent org's receipt footer text (dashboard
org settings). `None` → the POS prints its default footer.

require_table_for_orders.description:
Whether every dine-in sale here must belong to a table. Same shape as
the tax overrides: `null` inherits the organisation, which is not the
same as `false`. An explicit `false` lets a counter with two stools by
the window keep ringing walk-ups while the org's dining rooms seat
everyone; an explicit `true` does the reverse. This is the OVERRIDE —
the resolved answer is `branches::policy::require_table_for_orders`.

standard_float.description:
The drawer's standard opening float in minor units; drives the till
report's `standard_float` / `suggested_safe_drop`. `null` = none set.

tax_rate.description:
Tax policy OVERRIDES. `null` means inherit the organisation's setting —
which is not the same as `0`. An org that changes its rate still moves
every branch that never asked to differ; a branch that genuinely charges
no tax says so with an explicit `0`.

is_available.description: False disables the addon at this branch (excluded from the branch addon list).

price_override.description: Branch price in piastres; null inherits the org default_price.
Branch price in piastres; null inherits the org default_price.

revenue_by_method.description:
Goods only, by method actually tendered — money in. Tips are in
`total_tips`; refunds are not netted from the buckets.

total_tips.description: Tips, standalone — same definition as on the branch sales + shift reports.

auto_reject_minutes.description:
Minutes a `received` order may wait for a teller before the sweeper
rejects it and tells the customer. `null` = never: the order waits until
someone acts on it. Read at sweep time rather than frozen on the order,
so a branch that shortens it means the change to apply to what is
already waiting.

in_mall_discount_id.description:
Optional discount applied to each channel's item subtotal (reuses the
org `discounts` table). Frozen onto the order at intake. `null` = none.

in_mall_require_location.description:
When false, in-mall orders may be placed without a device GPS location
("confirm you're at the branch"). Shop/company + floor + unit are always
required regardless. Default true.

otp_required.description:
When false, the public checkout skips OTP phone verification for this
branch and accepts orders without a device token. Default true.

umbrella_fee.description: Flat per-branch fees (piastres). Pickup defaults to free.

by_default_decided.description: Suggestions the gender default decided, of those decided in the month.

gap_points.description:
The widest gap, in percentage points, between a gender's share of the
night shifts and its share of stated willingness (of headcount when
nobody stated any).

learning_frozen.description: Learning is paused at this branch: under 40% accepted over 4 weeks.

is_available.description: False disables the item at this branch (excluded from the branch menu).

price_override.description: Branch price in piastres; null inherits the org catalog base_price.

sizes.description: Per-size branch prices for this item (empty when none). Availability is item-level.

price_override.description: Branch price in piastres; null inherits the org catalog base_price.

sizes.description:
Per-size branch prices. `null`/omitted → leave existing size overrides untouched;
a list → REPLACE the item's size overrides with exactly that set (empty clears them).

BranchRules.description: A branch and which of its rules it overrides.

overridden.description: The fields this branch sets itself; every other one is the business's.

gross_sales.description:
Sales in range as rung up, before any refund. Was what `total_revenue`
meant until 2026-09.

refunded_amount.description:
Money refunded against the sales in range (partial refunds; a fully
refunded order is out of every figure here by status).

revenue_by_method.description:
Money collected FOR GOODS, bucketed by the method actually tendered
(`order_payments`) — money IN. Tips are not in here — see `total_tips`
— and refunds are not netted out: they are money OUT with a tender of
their own, on `GET /shifts/{id}/refunds` and the refunds dataset.

service_charge_waived_count.description:
Table bills in range whose service charge was waived, and what those
charges came to. Additive.

total_delivery_fees.description:
Delivery fees on the sales in range — inside `total_revenue`, outside
the tax base, not food revenue.

total_line_items.description:
Units sold (SUM of order_items.quantity) across non-voided orders in
range. Counts units, not distinct lines ("3× burger" contributes 3),
matching quantity_sold in the item/category breakdowns.

total_revenue.description:
What the sales in range are worth after refunds: `gross_sales` less
`refunded_amount`. A refund is attributed to the sale it was against,
whenever it was issued — the same restatement a full refund makes by
flipping the order's status out of the sold set.

total_service_charge.description:
Service charge on the dine-in bills in range, less what refunds took
back — inside `total_revenue` as the shop's income, not a pass-through.

total_tips.description:
Tips, standalone — never folded into a method bucket and never part of
`total_revenue`. Same definition as `total_tips` on the shift report, so
the two screens can be reconciled line for line.

auto_reject_minutes.description:
Minutes before an unaccepted order is rejected automatically. `null`
(and omitted, for older clients) = never.

in_mall_discount_id.description:
Optional per-channel discount ids (must be active discounts in the
caller's org). `null` clears the channel's discount.

in_mall_require_location.description:
When false, in-mall orders are accepted without a device GPS location.
Defaults to true so an omitting client keeps the location check on.

otp_required.description:
When false, the public checkout skips OTP for this branch. Defaults to
true so an omitting client keeps verification on.

price_override.description: Branch price for this size in piastres.

BranchStockRow.description:
One catalog ingredient as seen from a branch. Every live catalog ingredient
appears exactly once; `has_activity = false` means the branch has never
moved or counted it (on hand is 0 and every date is null).

cost_per_unit.description:
This branch's actual (weighted-average) cost, falling back to the org
standard cost. Piastres per unit; `null` ⟺ unknown.

last_counted_at.description: Last finalized stock count that included this ingredient; `null` = never.

last_movement_at.description: Last ledger movement of any kind; `null` = never.

on_hand.description: Book stock in the base unit. May be negative (sold past zero, flagged).

par_min.description: Reorder point: below-par when `on_hand <= par_min` and `par_min > 0`.

oneOf.description:
Optional one-time manager approval (the ordinary `ReplayApproval`
shape, as `live_approval` carries on an order, a refund or a waste).
Additive: without it the call behaves exactly as before.

flag_ids.description:
Every open flag to resolve at once — a till, a day, or a hand-picked
selection. Order does not matter; each id is its own transaction.

pending.description: An id this call could not resolve, and why. Never silently dropped.

resolved.description:
Ids that are now reviewed (already reviewed counts as resolved too —
resubmitting the same batch never fails or double-records).

oneOf.description:
Asset refs (WebP variants, signed); absent when the bundle has no asset
group. Additive: `image_url` keeps its legacy value.

item_cost.description:
Cost of the component (at its base size) in piastres. When
`item_cost_missing` is true this is a PARTIAL figure (unknown = 0 on the
wire for old-client compat) — display it as unknown, not as money.

item_cost_missing.description: True when the component's cost could not be fully resolved.

computed_cost.description:
Sum of the KNOWN component costs × quantity, in piastres. When
`cost_missing` is true this is a partial rollup (old-wire semantics) —
render it as unknown, never as 0.

cost_missing.description: True when at least one component's cost is unknown.

CampaignEffectivenessRow.description:
One outreach campaign's return-on-nudge: did the member earn again within
30 days of the message.

restore_inventory.description:
true (default): ingredients stay available. false: the food was made and is
wasted — the frozen plan is deducted from stock and logged as `waste`.

editable.description: Can the caller change this row for this person?

source.description: Where the answer comes from: owner | core | allow | deny | role | none.

CardBrand.description:
How a tenant's card should look.

Every field is optional and the site falls back to Madar's own palette, so a
tenant who has set nothing still gets a finished card rather than an
unstyled one. `org_name` is NOT optional: whose card this is must always be
on it, however little else has been configured.

card_image_url.description:
The wide photograph across the card — Apple's strip, Google's hero
image, and the band at the top of the web card. Absent is a finished
card, not a broken one.

logo_is_mark.description:
True when the logo is a shape on transparency, so the card may repaint
it in the foreground for contrast. False for a logo with its background
baked in, which gets a plate to sit on instead — repainting that one
would give a solid rectangle. See `orgs::branding::is_mark`.

program_name.description: What the programme calls itself ("Rewards", "Bean Club").

social_links.description:
Where else to find the shop, in the order a card prints them. Empty is
the common case, and the page draws nothing for it — no row, no
placeholder.

NOT gated on the branding tier, like `OrgBrand::social_links` it is read
from: a shop's Instagram is a fact about the shop in the way its name
is, so a Madar-coloured card carries the links too.

CardPreferences.description:
What a customer can change about their own card, without an account.

The token in the URL is the credential — the same one their pass carries and
the till scans. That is deliberate: a person who has just been messaged must
be able to stop the messages by tapping the link in the message, not by
remembering a password they never made.

locale.description:
The language they are reading this page in.

Sent by the page itself rather than chosen in a form. We stored whatever
their phone said at signup, and a phone that has since changed language
is a customer still being written to in the wrong one. Opening their own
card is the moment we can tell.

marketing_opt_out.description:
Stop sending marketing. Covers the birthday greeting as well as the
win-back: someone asking us to stop is asking the SHOP to stop, not to
be excluded from one campaign.

CardView.description:
The member's own card page — what they see when they open the link again.

The token in the path is the member's secret, which is why this returns only
what the pass already shows and never the phone number in full.

brand.description: Whose card this is, and how it should look.

marketing_opt_out.description: They have asked this shop to stop sending them things.

order_now_url.description:
"Order now": the ordering page, opened knowing who this is. Present only
when public ordering is configured and the shop takes online orders —
render the primary button when it is there, nothing when it is not.

progress_to_next.description: Progress towards the next one, after the earned ones are set aside.

rewards_ready.description: Rewards the balance has already earned — a card does not stop at full.

CartLineInput.description:
One line of a public cart. Prices are NOT taken from the client — the server
resolves them. `addons` reuses [`AddonInput`] but its `unit_price` is ignored.

shift_id.description: DEPRECATED: same value as `till_id` (kept for POS v0.5.1/v0.6.0).

CashMovementKind.description: What a cash movement IS, which fixes its sign.

expense_advance_to.description:
A pay-out handed to an employee for shop purchases: logged in Dawam as
their expense advance, never deducted (AV-8).

CatalogSyncResponse.description: The full catalog snapshot for a POS device.

changed.description:
`false` when `since` equals the current revision (client is up to date;
`items`/`ingredients` are then empty). `true` ⇒ the full payload follows.

display_order.description:
Drag-and-drop position (lower first); ties break on name. Set via
`PUT /categories/order`.

oneOf.description: Asset refs (Track B4, §11.10); null when no asset or not attached by this endpoint.

Sent first. Carries the conversation id when RESUMING one, so a client
can bind the stream immediately; `null` when starting a new conversation,
because it is created lazily on the first turn that produces something —
the id then arrives on the `answer` frame.
A model call is in flight. `step` counts from 1.
A query is about to run. Carries what it is, not its results.
A query came back. The block is identical to one in the final payload.
The finished turn — the same body `/ai/chat` returns.
The turn failed. A client should render this, not retry blindly.

ChatFrame.description:
One frame of a streamed turn.

Every variant except `Answer`/`Clarify`/`Incomplete` is progress and may be
ignored. Deliberately coarse: emitting the model's partial tokens would mean
streaming text that has not been through pseudonym restoration yet, and a
half-restored name is exactly what must never render.

accuracy_meters.description: The fix's reported accuracy, metres (CL-9: a perfect one is suspicious).

is_mock.description: The OS's mock-location marker for this fix (CL-9).

latitude.description: Device coordinates. Required whenever the org enforces the geofence.

oneOf.description: Set when the punch was queued offline; the server rebuilds its time (CL-11).

tracking_off.description:
"Always" location was refused: the shift is marked and the manager told
(CL-5). Location at the punch is still required.

is_mock.description: The OS's mock-location marker for this fix (CL-9).

oneOf.description: Set when the punch was queued offline; the server rebuilds its time (CL-11).

ClientSeen.description: One device (or device-less client) as last seen.

app_version.description:
From an `X-Madar-Client` of the form `<app>/<semver>` only; `null` for
the dashboard and for any client identified by its User-Agent.

client.description: `X-Madar-Client`; else `dashboard` for a browser; else the User-Agent.

device_code.description: The registered device's code, when the device is registered.

legacy_kinds.description: Every legacy kind this client has hit.

held_orders_left_open.description:
Held orders (and open counter carts) still parked on the device when
the teller chose to close anyway, and their total. Additive; older
tills omit them.

reconciliation.description: Absent (old clients) → every used method is stored `unreviewed`.

Column.description:
One output column: the SQL alias (also the JSON key on every row) plus how
to render it.

label.description: Human label for a header or legend.

ColumnKind.description:
The renderable kind of an output column, so a client can format it and pick
a sensible chart without knowing anything about the underlying SQL.

ComputedPayslip.description:
One employee's pay for a period, computed but not yet written.

PREVIEW AND GENERATE SHARE THIS. The preview endpoint exists so a manager can
see what payroll is about to do — a figure that would be worthless if it came
from a second implementation that could drift from the real one. So the
generator computes these first and then persists them, and the preview
computes exactly the same values and persists nothing.

advance_installment_piastres.description:
What the advances WANT versus what the payslip can afford differ when net
pay would go negative; this is the affordable figure, the one collected.

base_piastres.description:
After the calendar-day proration — what the days employed earn, at
each day's salary (PAY-13).

base_salary_piastres.description: The monthly salary in force at the end of the window.

breakdown.description:
Line-by-line, so a preview can name each deduction rather than showing a
lump sum nobody can argue with.

carry_out_piastres.description:
Deductions beyond what was earned: the payslip stops at zero and this
carries into the next one as a debt (PAY-12).

salary_missing.description:
On payroll with no salary set (owner decision D9): everything prices
at 0, and approval is refused (409 SALARY_MISSING) until the owner
sets it or marks them not on payroll.

consumed_value.description: Consumption valued in piastres; `null` if any contributing cost unknown.

latitude.description: The fence centre, so the phone can say inside/outside offline.

advance_cap_piastres.description:
Their salary-advance cap, decided by the server (AV-5, AT-3); shown
under the same visibility as the salary.

advance_within_cap.description:
What they owe in salary advances is within the cap; never hidden, so
a manager sees "within cap" / "over cap" without the figure (D7).

base_salary_piastres.description:
Only for people whose pay the caller may see (null too when no
salary is set: `salary_set`).

role.description:
`owner` · `manager` · `employee` (from the linked account; an employee
with no account is `employee`).

salary_set.description: A salary is on file (D9); false = "not set". Never hidden.

user_id.description: Their Madar account, when they have one.

rules_saved.description: The business saved its rules; nobody clocks in before (RU-1, DSH-6).

rules_saved_at.description:
When the rules were first saved; null until then. The sweep never
marks absent (or charges) a shift that started before it (B-SETUP-5),
so neither does the app (B-ONB-1).

condensed.description:
The running summary of everything before the verbatim window. Returned
so the UI can show what was condensed instead of a silent gap.

ConversationSummary.description: A conversation without its turns, for the list view.

compacted.description:
True once older turns have been folded into a summary — surfaced so a
client can say "earlier messages condensed" rather than appearing to
have lost them.

CoverageNeed.description: One band of the weekly coverage grid.

department_id.description: Only people of this department count toward it.

derived.description: What POS sales suggest, one-hour bands, when POS is on.

source.description:
What the engine uses: `grid` (typed), `pos` (derived from sales) or
`pattern` (the standing pattern's own coverage).

oneOf.description: `pos` (default) | `kds` | `waiter`

label.description: A name for the tablet it is meant for ("Front counter").

installments.description: Defaults to 1 — repaid in full from the next payslip.

force.description: Create even when no table fits (the booking shows as "needs a table").

table_ids.description: Explicit tables (skips auto-assignment). Empty = deliberately none.

geo_radius_meters.description: Geofence radius in meters. Defaults to 200.

printer_port.description: TCP port for the receipt printer. Defaults to `9100` if absent.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name. If absent, the branch inherits the org's timezone.

branch_id.description: The single branch this credential may read.

username.description: Basic-auth username. Unique across all orgs, case-insensitively.

branch_id.description: The branch where the customer was added (a till sends its own).

id.description: Client-minted id; a repeat with the same id returns the stored customer.

loyalty_customer_id.description:
DEPRECATED and ignored: a membership shares the customer's id, so there
is nothing to link. Accepted so deployed tills keep working.

source.description:
Where the customer came from. Defaults to `pos` when a branch is named
(a till) and `dashboard` otherwise.

file_url.description: A path returned by the existing `/uploads` endpoints.

CreateEmployeeRequest.description: Add an employee of any kind (see the module docs).

app_access.description: May sign in to the staff app. Defaults to "has a phone".

base_salary_piastres.description: Piastres. Ignored without `hr.payroll.edit` for every branch.

branch_ids.description: Where they work (at least one). `branch_id` is the older one-branch form.

phone.description: Their WhatsApp number: how they sign in to the staff app.

user_id.description:
Make this existing Madar user an employee (kind `linked`). Their name
and number are the defaults for the employee's.

CreateFloorTransferRequest.description:
Operational table-state edit from the POS: the layout (geometry/shape) is
dashboard-authored, but STATE — status walks (bussing a dirty table) and
which zone the physical table currently sits in — belongs to the floor
staff. Both fields optional; `clear_section` moves the table out of every
section (`section_id` wins when both are sent).

id.description: Client-minted id (offline-first identity; retries dedup on it).

target_section_id.description: The wish: any table in this section…

target_table_id.description: …or exactly this table. At least one of the two is required.

legacy_addon_type.description:
The legacy addon type this group is presented as to OLD clients through
the compat shim (the managed addon-type dropdown, e.g. `milk_type` /
`coffee_type` / `extra`). Swap-family behavior keys on it. `null` = a
custom group with no legacy lineage — INVISIBLE to old clients (the shim
projects `type` from this value, and the old wire requires it), so set
it whenever the pre-teardown fleet must see the group's options.

swap_category_id.description: Required meaning for `effect = swaps`: the ingredient category swapped.

slug.description: Optional explicit slug (`[a-z0-9_]`); derived from the name when omitted.

booking_id.description:
The booking this party arrived under: the ticket links to it and the
booking moves to `seated` in the same transaction.

customer_id.description:
The customer this bill is for, when the waiter picked one. Honoured when
the actor holds `customers.attach`; a merged id resolves and an unknown
one is ignored — a bill is never refused over its customer. Absent, a
bill opened for a booking takes the booking's customer.

discount_id.description: Optional discount the waiter applied at order time (overridable at settle).

idempotency_key.description: Client-minted dedup key for the ticket (exactly-once across LAN + cloud).

items.description: Client-priced items (same shape as a POS order line) — recorded verbatim.

round_idempotency_key.description: Per-round dedup key for the first round.

customer_id.description:
A manual customer (phase 6), attached when the actor holds
`customers.attach`. A merged id resolves; an unknown one is ignored —
a sale is never refused over its customer.

device_code.description: The device's code; with `device_id` + `order_number` the number is stored verbatim.

discount_applied_by.description:
Who put the discount on the sale (the signed-in till person). Read on
replay only; live, it is the caller. Additive.

discount_approval_id.description:
The manager approval (`approval.id` on the replay envelope) that let
the discount past the person's cap. Additive.

discount_kind.description:
Which discount act this is: `preset` | `manual_amount` | `manual_percent`.
Absent (older clients): a `discount_id` means preset, an ad-hoc discount
is manual of its type. Additive.

discount_percent_bps.description: The percentage asked for, in basis points (1250 = 12.5%). Additive.

oneOf.description:
A manager's one-time PIN approval for the LIVE route (owner,
2026-09-17): the offline queue has always carried an `approval` on the
replay envelope; this is the same object, sent with the live request
instead, so a live over-cap discount need not queue to be approved.
Verified the same way replay verifies one; `discount_approval_id`
above is set from its `id` once verified. Additive.

loyalty_customer_id.description:
The loyalty member spending a balance on this sale. Required when
`loyalty_redemptions` is non-empty, and ONLY for that: earning is a
separate, later act (`POST /loyalty/award`), so a sale that redeems
nothing never names a member here.

loyalty_redemptions.description:
Rewards covering lines of this cart. Each names a line by its index in
`items` and how many of that line's units the reward pays for, so a
mixed basket can have one free coffee among four paid ones.

order_number.description:
The device's own order number (contract R4): its per-business-day
sequence, the same counter as the `NNNN` of its `order_ref`. Stored
VERBATIM when the request also names `device_id` and a non-blank
`device_code` — the order then reads `display_number` `<device_code>-<n>`.
Without all three (old clients, dashboard, delivery) it is ignored and the
server numbers the sale per till: `MAX(order_number)+1` over the till's
server-numbered orders, under the till advisory lock
(`uq_orders_till_legacy_number`).

order_ref.description:
Client-minted order reference (`<BRANCH>-<YYMMDD>-<DEVICE>-<NNNN>`). Stored
verbatim when present; absent → the server mints the deterministic
shift-based ref. The global `UNIQUE(order_ref)` index keeps both paths
collision-safe (a managed per-device code makes concurrent tills unique).

service_mode.description:
Where the drink is going: `"takeaway"` (default) or `"dine_in"`. NOT
`order_type`: that is derived from whether a waiter's ticket was settled
and decides the service charge. This says only whether the customer is
drinking in — so a counter shop with no floor can say it — and its only
effect is that packaging (cups, lids, straws) is not deducted from
stock. Absent ⇒ takeaway, which is what every client before this did.

started_by.description:
The person who started this sale's cart, when the till says it was not
the person ringing it (a held order resumed after a teller switch).
Recorded when it names someone of the same org; anything else is
dropped with a warning, never refused. Additive; older tills omit it.

verification.description: `server` | `lan` | `unverified` — the till's verification as the device knew it.

logo.description:
Logo image file. PNG, JPEG, or WebP. Optional — omit the field
entirely to create the org without a logo.

require_table_for_orders.description: Must every sale name a table? Default false.

service_charge_rate.description: A fraction, like the tax rate: 0.12 is 12%. Default 0.

service_charge_taxable.description: Is the service charge itself taxed? Default true.

tax_inclusive.description: Are menu prices tax-inclusive? Default false (tax added on top).

tax_rate.description: A FRACTION: 0.14 is 14%. Same unit as `PATCH /orgs/{id}`.

template.description: Role template the org starts from: `restaurant` (default) or `cafe`.

amount.description:
Minor units, > 0. Together with every refund already on the order it
may not exceed `orders.total_amount`.

client_ref.description:
Client-minted idempotency key. A retried request or a replayed offline
queue carrying the same key gets the original refund back instead of
handing the money out again.

device_id.description: The device issuing the refund (else the `X-Madar-Device` header).

issued_at.description:
When the refund was issued. Omit for live requests — the server stamps
`now()`. An offline till sends the real time; future values are rejected.

oneOf.description:
A manager's on-the-spot unlock for a refund over the issuer's own
`max_amount` (the teller default is 0, so every refund asks). Additive.

method.description:
How the money went back — a name from the org's payment-method
vocabulary. One tender per refund; a split is two refunds.

order_id.description: The settled sale the money goes back against.

till_id.description:
The shift whose drawer the money leaves. Omit for a live request and the
actor's own open shift at the order's branch is used; a replayed offline
refund must name the shift it was issued in, the way a queued sale does.

copy_from.description: Start from this role's grants; otherwise from the default template.

attendance_record_id.description: `correction` only — the record whose punch is wrong.

employee_id.description: Admin-only. Omitted on `/staff/me/*`, where it is always the caller.

is_paid.description:
Only when the request is approved as it is filed (the filer holds
`hr.requests.self_approve`): leave paid or unpaid — REQUIRED for such a
leave (400 `LEAVE_PAY_REQUIRED`, RQ-2) — and an excuse's pay (omitted:
the rule decides).

leave_half.description:
`first` | `second`: which half of the day a half-day leave takes off.
Omitted on a half day = the first.

leave_type_id.description: Deprecated (RQ-2): ignored. Leave has no types.

title.description: A mission's title; when omitted the note is used.

to_time.description:
Branch-local wall clock. An excuse ending at or before it starts runs
past midnight.

work_shift_id.description:
The shift a late arrival, early departure or excuse is for. Omitted =
the shift of the day its time falls in.

category_id.description: Cycle-count scope: only ingredients in this category.

branch_ids.description:
Branches to assign the new user to immediately. Branch managers
can only assign to branches they themselves are assigned to.

email.description: Required for admins and managers; ignored for tellers.

password.description:
Required when `role` is anything other than `teller`. Plain text;
hashed server-side with bcrypt before storage.

pin.description:
Required when `role = teller`. A NEW PIN is exactly 6 ASCII digits
(owner decision, 2026-09-16); PINs already in use keep working at their
old length. Ask `GET /users/pin-suggestion` for a free one.

reason.description:
expired | spoiled | damaged | overproduction | order_cancelled | theft | other
(`order_cancelled` is normally auto-logged by void/cancel, not entered here)

last_used_at.description: Last successful authentication, or null if the partner has never pulled.

CredentialWithSecret.description:
Returned ONLY by create and rotate. The secret is bcrypt-hashed on the way
in and is not recoverable afterwards, so the dashboard must show it once and
tell the operator to copy it.

missing_salary_count.description:
People on payroll with no salary set (D9): the preview rows with
`salary_missing`; approval is refused until it is 0.

paid_count.description: How many payslips are marked paid (a 'none' mark counts).

payslips.description: The frozen payslips once it has been generated.

preview.description: A live computation while the period is still a draft.

totals.description: The run added up by the server (AT-3).

is_member.description: A live loyalty membership exists for this customer (same id).

loyalty_customer_id.description:
DEPRECATED, kept for one release: a loyalty membership now shares the
customer's id, so this is `id` when `is_member` and null otherwise.

source.description:
Where the customer first came from: `pos`, `online`, `loyalty`,
`booking`, `table_qr`, `aggregator` or `dashboard`.

total_spent.description: Sum of completed sales, minor units.

CustomerAddress.description: A place a customer has had an order sent to.

branch_id.description: The branch it was last ordered from.

channel.description: The channel it was last used with: `in_mall`, `outside` or `umbrella`.

resolved_from.description: Set when the id asked for was merged: the id that was asked for.

help.description: What one row is, and when to use this dataset instead of another.

DateSet.description: A person's date that holds its own set (a date change), not the pattern.

day_off.description: The date is a day off by date change (it holds no shift).

DayBlock.description: One block on a date, with its own from/to if it has one.

DayTime.description: A block's own start/end on one weekday, on top of its default times.

end_time.description: At or before the start = ends the next day.

DayView.description: One person's date after a change.

follows_pattern.description: The date follows the standing pattern (no date change).

shifts.description: Empty = a day off (or nothing rostered).

warnings.description: Labour limits the person's week now goes past. Warnings, never blocks.

reason.description:
Why. Required to reject (400 `REASON_REQUIRED`, D8); optional to
approve.

impact.description: Measured after-window aggregate; `null` until ≥1 day of after-data.

impact_complete.description: True once the full baseline window has elapsed since the decision.

DeductionOverrideEvent.description:
One waive, unwaive or override of a payroll deduction, from the money
audit log (D8).

amount_before_piastres.description:
What the line charged before and after this event (a waiver: after
0; undoing one: before 0).

effective_date.description:
The line itself: its day, what made it (`absence`, `late_penalty`,
…) and its rule's reason code. Null if the line is gone.

DeliveryAddonOption.description:
One option in the org-wide addon catalog. The catalog is global (the POS
model): every item can use any addon; swap-vs-additive is decided server-side
from the addon `type` + the item recipe at order time. `price` is the
channel-effective surcharge in piastres (branch_channel → branch → catalog
default). Channel-unavailable options are excluded from the catalog entirely.

DeliveryChannelSales.description:
Delivery sales for one delivery channel. Revenue and order counts are over
**delivered** orders only; `cancelled_orders` is shown separately so the UI
can surface drop-off without inflating revenue.

Read from `delivery_orders` — the quote — not from `orders`: a delivery that
never settled into a sale still tells the shop something about its
channels. Refunds are against the sale and are not netted here.

delivery_fees.description:
Sum of `delivery_fee` (piastres) over delivered orders. Outside the tax
base and not food revenue; a pickup carries none.

goods_revenue.description:
`revenue − delivery_fees`: the bill for the goods (tax included), the
figure comparable with dine-in and takeaway revenue.

revenue.description:
Sum of `total` (piastres) over delivered orders on this channel — the
whole bill, delivery fee included.

addons.description:
Org-wide addon catalog (global, POS model): channel-effective, grouped by
`type`, applicable to every item. Channel-unavailable options are excluded.

oneOf.description:
The active discount for this channel (customer-facing) or `null`. Applies
to the item subtotal only — the delivery fee is always charged in full.

DeliveryMenuDiscount.description:
Customer-facing summary of a channel's active discount, so the public UI can
tell the customer "you've got X off" and show a discounted estimate.

value.description:
LEGACY SPELLING — an integer, 0-100 for a percentage; piastres for
`fixed`. See `discounts::wire`.

value_rate.description: The stored fraction, for clients that know to ask.

allowed_addon_ids.description:
Explicit per-item addon allowlist (IDs from `menu_item_allowed_addons`).
When non-empty the customizer filters the global catalog to these IDs by
default, with a "show all" escape hatch. Empty = no restriction.

default_milk_addon_id.description:
The item's base/default milk: the `milk_type` addon whose ingredient
matches the item recipe's milk ingredient. The online customizer
pre-selects it (mirrors the POS default-milk selection). `None` when the
item has no milk in its recipe or no matching milk addon exists.

modifier_groups.description:
The item's modifier groups (unified model), channel-effective. Empty ⇒
the customizer falls back to `addons` + `allowed_addon_ids`.

DeliveryModifierGroup.description:
A per-item modifier group from the unified model (`menu_item_modifier_groups`
→ `modifier_groups`/`modifier_options`), constraints resolved (attachment
overrides beat group defaults) and options already filtered to the
attachment's `included_option_ids`. Only addon-sourced options appear here —
the item's priced optionals stay in `optionals`. Empty until the org's
catalog is backfilled onto the unified tables; the customizer falls back to
the flat `addons` catalog + `allowed_addon_ids` in that case.

addon_type.description:
The group's legacy addon type (`milk_type` / `coffee_type` / `extra` /
custom) — the swap-family hint the customizer keys its delta-price
estimate on. `None` for groups with no legacy lineage.

DeliveryModifierOption.description:
One option inside a per-item modifier group. `option_id` is the STABLE id —
it equals the legacy `addon_item_id`, so order intake accepts it unchanged in
`addons[].addon_item_id` (menu-unification stable-id rule).

price.description:
Channel-effective surcharge (piastres): branch_channel → branch →
channel → catalog default. Unavailable options are excluded entirely.

DeliveryOptionalField.description:
A per-item optional toggle (e.g. "Extra hot", "No sugar"). `price` is the
piastres surcharge; `size_label` is set when the optional only applies to a
specific size.

address_id.description: The saved address it was sent to, when it was saved.

cart.description: The frozen priced line snapshot the POS renders before finalize.

contact_override.description: "Ordered by X for Y": the snapshot phone is not the customer's own.

customer_id.description:
The customer this order belongs to (design §2.5). `customer_name` and
`customer_phone` beside it are the SNAPSHOT — what was typed, what the
driver calls — and stay as they were whatever happens to the customer.
`None` for an order from before customers existed whose phone is not a
valid number.

discount_id.description:
Frozen channel discount on the item subtotal. `discount_amount` is 0
when none.

discount_rate.description:
The stored value — a fraction for a percentage. Same column as
[`DeliveryOrder::discount_value`].

discount_value.description:
LEGACY SPELLING on the wire — an integer, 0-100 for a percentage. See
`discounts::wire`: a double here fails to deserialise the whole
DELIVERY ORDER on every shipped till, not just this field.

distance_source.description:
How `road_distance_meters` was measured: `osrm` (routed) or `haversine`
(straight line — the routing fallback, and always the in-mall walking
distance). `None` exactly when no distance was recorded.

extra_prep_minutes.description: Extra prep minutes the teller added on top of the branch base (multiples of 5).

payment_method.description:
What was actually taken at the door. Set at finalize and only then;
`Some` exactly when the order is `delivered`.

payment_method_hint.description: What the customer SAID they would pay with, at checkout. Display only.

service_charge_amount.description:
Always 0: the service charge is dine-in only. Present so the till can
render the same breakdown for every kind of sale.

tax_amount.description:
The tax as priced at intake, under the policy frozen beside it. Inside
`total` when `tax_inclusive`, added to it otherwise. Finalize does not
re-price: a rate the shop changes between the quote and the door does
not move a bill the customer already agreed.

tax_inclusive.description:
Copy of the ONE inclusivity flag (org, branch override) as it stood at
intake — not a setting of its own.

total.description:
The quote: `subtotal - discount_amount + delivery_fee`, plus
`tax_amount` when the tax is exclusive. Replayed verbatim at finalize.

contact_device_token.description:
A one-time order to a different phone, at a branch that requires OTP:
the device token proving THAT phone.

device_token.description:
Device-trust token from OTP verify (proves the phone). With
`member_token` it must prove the CUSTOMER's phone, not the typed one.

identity_change.description:
What a typed name/phone that differs from the customer's MEANS:
`"one_time"` (ordering for someone else: the order's snapshot carries
the typed contact, the profile is untouched) or `"update_name"` (correct
the stored name). A different PHONE with no choice is refused with 409
`IDENTITY_CHOICE_REQUIRED` (`kind: "phone"`); a different name alone
defaults to one-time. Ignored without `member_token`.

member_token.description:
Ordering from a loyalty card ("order now"): the order belongs to the
card's customer whatever name and phone are typed. The server compares
the typed contact with the customer's and classifies the difference —
see `identity_change`.

payment_method_hint.description: "cash" | "card" — a hint the teller can change at finalize.

save_address.description:
Keep the address on the customer's profile. Defaults to yes for an
ordinary order and to NO for a one-time order for someone else.

DeliverySalesReport.description:
Delivery sales rolled up across channels, plus a per-channel breakdown.
Always returns every channel in [`DELIVERY_CHANNELS`] (zero-filled) so the
dashboard renders a stable shape.

DeliveryTracking.description:
Customer-safe tracking view of a delivery order, keyed by its opaque UUID
(same capability-URL trust model as the device-token flow). No phone number
is exposed; the destination fields are the customer's own inputs. Powers the
public `/track/{id}` page (polled, since the public surface has no SSE).

estimated_prep_minutes.description: Branch base prep time + the teller's per-order addition (minutes).

tax_amount.description:
The tax line, frozen at intake. Inside `total` when `tax_inclusive`
(render "includes VAT"), added to it otherwise (render a tax line).

employee_count.description: Live employees currently assigned. Not stored.

manager_name.description: Denormalised for the dashboard list; not stored.

code_conflict.description: Another live device at the same branch uses the same code.

DeviceKind.description:
OpenAPI-only vocabulary for `devices.kind` (CHECK `kind IN ('pos','kds','waiter')`).
The struct fields stay `String`, so the wire strings are unchanged.

Dir.description: Sort direction. `Asc` is what unlocks "worst", "slowest", "least" questions.

covered_by_others.description:
Their own shifts a colleague covered (not rejected): the absence stays
theirs (CV-6), this says someone stepped in.

covers_given.description:
Colleagues' shifts this person covered, confirmed by a manager (CV-7).
A cover is never a present day of the coverer's own.

covers_pending.description: Covers still waiting for the manager.

department_id.description: `None` for a person with no department set — grouped as "Unassigned".

rank_in_department.description:
1 = best in this department: fewest absences, then fewest lates, then
least total late time. Ties share a rank (SQL `RANK()`), so a
department where everyone has a clean record is all `1`s.

value.description:
LEGACY SPELLING — an integer, 0-100 for a percentage, minor units for
`fixed`. What every shipped client was generated against; see
`discounts::wire`. Read [`Discount::value_rate`] for the real stored
number.

value_rate.description:
The stored value: a FRACTION for `percentage` (0.14 = 14%, like every
other rate in this schema), or minor units for `fixed`. The same
column as [`Discount::value`], spelled the way the engine holds it.

DiscountAuditEntry.description: One discounted sale in the discounts audit.

applied_by_name.description: Who applied it (the till operator for older sales).

flagged.description:
The sale was replayed with a discount its author was not allowed and
no valid manager approval (`authz_replay_flags`).

EarningItem.description: One item that collects, denormalised for the picker the same way a reward is.

base_price.description:
Menu price in piastres. Shown so an admin picking items can see what
they are handing a stamp for.

EarningItemList.description: The list in force at a scope, and whether it came from the org.

inherited.description: True when these rows are the org's rather than this branch's own.

items.description: Empty means EVERY item collects — not that nothing does.

advance_cap_piastres.description:
The owner's cap on what this person may owe in salary advances, in
piastres (AV-5): the server's figure, so no client recomputes it.
Hidden with the salary.

advance_within_cap.description:
What they owe in salary advances (pending ones counted) is within the
cap. Never hidden: what a manager sees instead of the cap (D7).

app_access.description: May sign in to the staff app with a WhatsApp code.

base_salary_piastres.description:
`None` when the caller may not read this person's pay — see the module
docs — or when no salary is set (`salary_set` tells the two apart).

branch_ids.description: Where they work; managers see the people of their branches (RO-6).

cant_work_days.description: Days they can't work: 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday.

device_model.description: The live phone signed in to the staff app, if any.

gender.description: `m` · `f` · null — only ever a soft default for late shifts (SC-13).

kind.description:
`linked` · `app` (signs in to the staff app, no Madar account) ·
`manual` (records only, no app).

on_payroll.description:
Paid through Dawam (the default). Off for someone who uses the app
and is rostered but is not paid here (an owner, say): the payroll
run, the estimate and the payslips skip them.

role.description: The linked user's POS role; null for an unlinked employee.

salary_set.description:
A salary is on file (owner decision D9): false = "not set" (someone a
manager added or imported), shown as "—" and flagged by payroll.
Never hidden: it says nothing about the amount.

user_id.description:
The linked Madar user, when this employee is one (a cashier, a manager,
the owner). Null for someone who is only on payroll.

ErrorBody.description:
Wire shape of every error JSON. Keep in lockstep with
`AppError::error_response` below.

code.description:
Stable, machine-readable code for the error classes a client must branch
on programmatically (e.g. `ORG_SUSPENDED`). Omitted for the generic
cases where the status code alone is enough.

retry_after_seconds.description:
How long to wait before trying again, in seconds. Present on a
`PIN_THROTTLED` refusal, absent everywhere else, so the PIN pad can run
a countdown rather than inventing one.

till.description:
The till a `TILL_OPEN_AT_OTHER_BRANCH` / `TILL_OPEN_ELSEWHERE` refusal
is about (`TillBrief`). Omitted everywhere else.

vars.description:
The figures of a coded refusal (`CodedVars`), for the client's own
wording. Omitted everywhere else.

applies_here.description: For an assignment step: does the assignment cover the branch asked about?

grants.description: For an assignment step: does the role grant the capability?

kind.description:
owner | inactive | assignment | core | override_allow | override_deny |
protected | not_held | limit | ask_manager

suggested.description:
Suggestions for people of this gender decided in the month, and
accepted.

branches.description: The same, branch by branch, each with its own gap flag.

decided_4w.description: Suggestions managers decided in the last 4 weeks, and how many they accepted.

learning_frozen.description: Learning is paused at some branch.

rows.description: Night share by gender against stated willingness, the whole business.

help.description:
One line on exactly what it counts. Absent for dimensions, whose label
is self-explanatory.

payment_method.description: The actual method the customer paid (overrides the hint). Must be an org method.

oneOf.description:
The next active booking claiming this table (today's service, or the
one in progress). The floor renders "held" from `held_from` by its own
clock; nothing here is written to `status`. Only the list endpoint fills
it — single-row writes return `null`.

party_size.description:
How many sat down (covers) on the live occupancy, when the host counted
them or the bill carries a guest count. `null` when free or unknown.

seated_at.description:
When the party at this table sat down — the hold's stamp, else the
bill's opening. `null` unless the table is seated. Every device renders
its table clock from this, so they all agree.

table_id.description: The table the party actually moves to (must satisfy the wish).

is_return.description: true ⟹ a return to supplier (negative stock effect).

quantity.description: Base stock units received (+) or returned (−).

GoogleObjectDump.description: The card Google holds, plus the two counts that make it readable at a glance.

error.description: Why there is no object, in Google's words.

expected_locations.description: Branches this member's card should be pinned to, from our own side.

object.description: Google's object, untouched. `None` when the read itself failed.

stored_locations.description: Branches Google says are on it. A gap between the two is the answer.

class.description: The class as Google holds it now.

class_locations.description: Branches Google kept on the shop's class.

error.description: The first thing that went wrong, if anything did.

object.description: The object as Google holds it now.

object_locations.description: Branches Google kept on this member's object.

sent_locations.description: Branches this member's card was sent, from our side.

steps.description: Every request and Google's answer, in order.

Grain.description:
The *shape* of a result set, derived from the dimensions a query groups by.
This is what lets a dashboard render any metric with no per-metric code: a
scalar becomes a KPI card, a series becomes a line, a breakdown becomes a
bar or pie.

included_option_ids.description: `null` = offer all of the group's options; else the allowlisted subset.

GroupOptionOut.description:
A modifier option as returned by the reusable-group endpoints (org-scoped,
no per-item `included`/cost context — that belongs to the studio aggregate).

recipe.description: The option's recipe lines (base unit), ordered by ingredient name.

GroupOptionRecipeLine.description: One recipe line of a modifier option, as the group editor shows it.

size_label.description:
`null` = the generic line (every size); else the per-size amount for that
size label (menu modeling B9). The editor must round-trip it on save.

GroupOut.description: A reusable modifier group with its options (org-scoped catalog view).

swap_category_id.description: For `swaps`: the ingredient category whose recipe line each option replaces.

GroupUsageItem.description: One menu item a group is attached to, as the group editor lists it.

default_option_id.description:
Swap groups only: the option preselected on this item, i.e. the first offered
option (sort, name) carrying the recipe's ingredient of the swap category, on
the item's first size that has one. `null` for non-swap groups or when the
recipe's ingredient is not offered (lint F4 / F5).

included_option_ids.description: `null` = the item offers every option of the group.

is_required.description: Effective for this item: attachment override, else the group default.

warnings.description: Lint findings F4–F10 about this item and this group.

HistoryTurn.description:
One earlier exchange, in compact form.

Result *tables* are never replayed — they are large, and the model does not
need last week's rows to answer this week's question. What it does need is
the **query** that answered before, which is why `spec` is here: a follow-up
like "and last month?" or "same thing for Marina" is that spec with one
field changed. Prose alone forces the model to re-derive the whole query
from its own summary, which is exactly where a follow-up silently drifts
into answering a different question.

Clients get the spec back on every result block (`results[].spec`) and
should echo it here.

answer.description: What the assistant replied. Optional so a client can send a partial log.

oneOf.description:
The query that produced that answer, from `results[].spec`. Optional so
an older client, or a turn that ran no query, still works.

party_size.description:
How many people sat down (covers), as the host counted them. Recorded
on the hold and inherited by the bill's first round when it carries no
guest count of its own. Anything not positive is not recorded.

seated_at.description:
When the party actually sat down, by the till's clock. An offline seat
replays later than it happened; this keeps every device's table clock
on the seating. Clamped server-side to the last 12 hours, never in the
future, and never before the table's previous party left. Recorded only
-- it moves no status.

decision.description:
`holiday` (nobody marked absent; working it pays the multiplier) or
`dismissed` (a normal day).

decided_by.description: Who decided it and when (AT-10); null while undecided.

decision.description: null = not decided yet: a normal day unless set up (RU-10).

HoursEntry.description:
One weekly booking window. `dow`: 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday. `open`/`close`
are `HH:MM` local; a close at or before open means "closes after midnight".

is_packaging.description:
Cups, lids, straws: a dine-in sale skips every ingredient in a packaging
category. The slug `packaging` is treated as packaging too.

slug.description:
Stable machine key (`general`, `milk`, `coffee_bean`, …). `milk` and
`coffee_bean` carry swap semantics in the menu; the slug never changes.

variance_reason.description:
Why the count differs from book stock. One of: theft | spoilage |
breakage | miscount | supplier_short | transfer_error | other. Required
at finalize for rows whose difference exceeds the org's threshold.

ItemOptionInput.description:
One priced optional in the item's per-item `Options` set. `id` present ⇒ update
that option; absent ⇒ create a new one. `recipe` null ⇒ leave the option with no
recipe lines; else the replace-set of its lines.

recipe.description: `null` = keep no recipe; else the option's replace-set of recipe lines.

ItemOptionOut.description:
A priced optional — a member of the item-private `Options` group
(a modifier_group with `legacy_addon_type IS NULL` owned by this item).

JoinInfo.description: What the signup page needs to render itself before anyone types anything.

birthday_enabled.description:
Ask for a date of birth. False means the form does not show the field —
a shop that does not run birthday rewards is not given one to hold.

birthday_reward_amount.description:
What the birthday is worth here, so the page can say what it is FOR
rather than asking for a date of birth and explaining nothing.

branch_id.description:
Absent for an org-wide code — the customer has not told us where they
are, and nothing in the programme needs to know.

brand.description: Whose programme this is, and how the page should look.

earn_piastres_per_point.description:
EGP that earns one point — the page's "a point for every N EGP" line.
Piastres on the wire, as everywhere; the page divides by 100. Only
meaningful when `mode` is `"points"`.

enabled.description:
False when the program is off here — the page says so instead of taking
a signup that would go nowhere.

mode.description:
`"points"` (earned on spend) or `"visits"` (a stamp per order) — which
sentence the page writes.

next_reward_cost.description: The cheapest reward on offer, in `mode`'s currency.

require_otp.description: The page collects an OTP only when the branch asks for one.

rewards.description: The rewards on offer, each with what it costs.

birth_month.description:
The day of their birthday, 1–12 and 1–31. Accepted ONLY where the org
asked for one: a field the shop turned off must not be storable by
posting past the form.

No year, deliberately. A greeting needs to know WHEN, not how old — and
a full date of birth is an identity credential, which is a great deal
more than an annual message needs.

branch_id.description:
The branch whose counter code was scanned, when one was. Absent for an
org-wide code — see [`BranchQuery`].

device_token.description:
Device-trust token from `/public/otp/verify`. Required only when the
branch's `require_otp` is on.

locale.description: 'en' or 'ar' — the language the pass is written in.

JoinResult.description:
What the customer sees after signing up: their card, and the buttons — or,
for a phone that is already a member and has not been proved, an invitation
to prove it.

The member token is a bearer credential: whoever holds it holds the card,
the balance, the purchase history and the wallet passes. So it is handed out
on exactly two occasions — to a NEW member, whose token nobody else could
want yet, and to an existing member whose device has verified THIS phone by
