OTP. Typing a phone number is not proof of owning it; anyone who knows a
customer's number can type it.

already_member.description:
True when this phone was already a member — the page says "welcome back"
rather than pretending to have made a new card.

balance.description:
The live balance, in `mode`'s currency. Zero for a fresh member, and zero
(not the real figure) while `verify_required`.

card_link_sent.description:
While `verify_required`: the card link was also sent to the number on
file, by WhatsApp — the one channel that proves possession without a
code. False when no gateway is configured or there is no public base to
build a link on; the page then offers only the OTP.

member_token.description: Absent when `verify_required`: the page has nothing to show yet.

name.description:
The name as the caller typed it. For a returning member the name ON FILE
is not echoed until they have verified — it is a fact about the person
who owns the phone, not about the person typing it.

oneOf.description: Absent when `verify_required`.

verify_required.description:
This phone already has a card and the device has not proved it owns the
phone. The page should run the ordinary OTP flow (`/public/otp/request`
then `/public/otp/verify`) and POST here again with the `device_token`
it is handed; the card comes back on that call.

KitchenLine.description:
A slim kitchen display line (NO prices) — what the cook reads. Built from an
order item or a ticket round line by the caller.

KitchenTicketView.description: One fire event projected for the kitchen (a round or a counter order).

labour_piastres.description:
From the clock: worked minutes at each person's minute rate, plus the
overtime premium. The payslip stays the final word.

labour_share_bp.description: Labour as a share of sales, basis points (null with no sales).

LabourWarning.description: A roster past a labour limit. Warns, never blocks (RU-13).

date.description: The day (or, for a week's limit, the Saturday it starts).

LateDeductionKind.description: What a tier costs the employee.

LateTier.description:
One rung of the late-penalty ladder. Ranges are inclusive at both ends;
`to_minutes = None` is the open-ended top rung.

LedgerEntry.description: One line of a member's history.

basis_piastres.description: Piastres the rule was applied to (earns only).

created_by.description:
Who wrote the row: the teller who applied a reward or rang the sale, the
admin who adjusted by hand. `None` for the system (birthday, win-back,
a trigger with no actor).

currency.description: `"points"` or `"visits"` — which balance this row moved.

kind.description:
`earn`, `redeem`, `adjust`, or `reverse_earn` / `reverse_redeem` /
`reverse_adjust` — the last three undo the row named in `reverses_id`.

reverses_id.description: For a reversal, the row it undoes.

source.description:
Why the row exists: `sale`, `redemption`, `void`, `refund`, `birthday`,
`winback` or `manual`. What a till or a dashboard should print as the
reason, instead of guessing from the kind and the note.

below_target_gap.description:
Σ(target·revenue − margin) over below-target rows — "margin left on
the table" this period, in piastres.

cost_known.description: Cost summed over rows where it is known.

revenue_cost_unknown.description: Revenue sitting on rows whose cost is unknown (visibly reconciles).

LegacyTill.description: The removed drawer entity, synthesized one per branch for old settings screens.

LiabilityTrend.description:
A weekly trend of the programme's liability, in the org's live currency
(points or visits — never both; see [`PointsLiability`]).

`loyalty_customers.points_balance`/`visits_balance` are CURRENT balances
with no history table, so this is not a snapshot of the outstanding
balance at each week — it is each week's *net change* (earned minus
redeemed, reversals netted in), read straight off the ledger. Summing
`outstanding` across every week since the programme started would
reconstruct the current balance; a single week says whether that week
grew or shrank the liability.

outstanding.description:
Net points/visits change in that week (earn − redeem, reversals
netted in) — not a running balance. See [`LiabilityTrend`].

max_age_minutes.description: How old the thing acted on may be, in minutes.

own.description:
Only the person's own work. Absent means unrestricted, so a dashboard
that predates the field keeps meaning what it always meant.

LinkableUser.description: A Madar user who can be made an employee.

group_id.description: The modifier group the finding is about, when it is group-scoped.

item_id.description: The menu item the finding is about, when it is item-scoped.

size_label.description: Set when the finding is about one size of an item.

LoginRequest.description:
Login is dual-mode:

- **Email + password** (admins, managers, super-admins): supply
  `email` and `password`. `org_id` is optional — if provided, the
  user must belong to that org; if omitted, lookup is by email only.
- **PIN + name** (tellers): supply `name`, `pin`, and **`branch_id`**
  (required). The teller must be assigned to that branch. `org_id` is
  derived server-side from the branch — never trusted from the client.

branch_id.description: Required for PIN login. The org is derived from this branch server-side.

name.description:
The person's display name. Optional for PIN login: without it the PIN
alone identifies the person (PIN-only sign-in, org-wide unique PINs).
Old tablets send it and keep the name-narrowed lookup.

oneOf.description:
The person's open till at the branch they signed into (any device), so
the device can resume it or show where it is open.

require_table_for_orders.description:
Every dine-in sale belongs to a table.

The till needs this, not just the server: the rule changes what the POS
puts in front of a teller — the floor becomes the home screen and a sale
starts by picking a table — and a refusal AFTER the items are rung up is
far too late to be useful.

tax_policy.description:
The full policy, including tax-inclusive pricing and service charge.
Prefer this over the flat `tax_rate` above.

tax_rate.description:
Org tax rate as a decimal (e.g. 0.14 = 14% VAT); 0.0 when no org. Mirrors
/auth/me so the POS has it immediately after login.

token.description: JWT to send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on subsequent requests.

customer_id.description:
A member the till already identified, re-read before a charge so the
balance and catalogue it prices against are the server's current ones.

phone.description: Manual fallback for a customer whose phone is dead.

token.description: The token from the scanned pass barcode. Preferred.

par_max.description: Order-up-to level; `null` when only a reorder point is set.

par_min.description: Reorder point the item is at or below.

suggested_qty.description: Quantity to bring stock back to par_max (or par_min when no max is set).

supplier_id.description: Default supplier for this ingredient (for one-click "create PO"); may be null.

LoyaltyAnalytics.description:
The redemption report, computed in the database so a dashboard never loads
every member to draw it.

earned_points.description: Balance earned, net of clawbacks written in the range.

redeemed_points.description: Balance spent, net of reversals written in the range.

redeemed_value_minor.description: Minor units of goods given away as rewards, on sales not voided.

redemptions.description: Redemption rows in the range (one per covered order line).

refused_redemptions.description: Replayed sales whose rewards the points could not pay for.

LoyaltyBehavior.description:
Behavioral rates over the range — how much of the member base actually
uses the programme, not just what it's worth. `total_members` and
`members_ever_redeemed` are org-wide and lifetime (a balance/history isn't
branch-scoped); every other figure narrows to `branch_id` and the range,
same as [`LoyaltyAnalytics`].

active_member_rate.description: `active_members / total_members`. `0.0` when there are no members.

active_members.description:
Distinct (not deleted) members with any loyalty transaction in the
range — deleted members are left out of every count so no rate over
`total_members` can exceed 1.

members_ever_redeemed.description:
Distinct (not deleted) members who have ever redeemed a reward.
Org-wide, lifetime.

new_members_active.description: Active members who enrolled during the range.

one_time_members.description: Members with exactly 1 earning visit in the range.

redemption_ratio.description:
`redeemed_points_period / earned_points_period` — the share of what
was earned in the range that got spent in it. Points earned before the
range and redeemed inside it are not the numerator's earn, so this can
exceed 1.0 on a range with heavy redemption of an older balance.

repeat_members.description: Members with 2+ earning visits in the range.

repeat_visit_rate.description:
`repeat_members / (repeat_members + one_time_members)`. `0.0` when
nobody earned in the range.

returning_members_active.description: Active members who enrolled before the range started.

total_members.description: Enrolled, not deleted, as of now. Org-wide.

LoyaltyRedemptionInput.description: One reward applied to one line of the cart.

item_index.description:
Index into `items`. An index rather than an id because a cart may hold
the same menu item on two lines with different modifiers, and only the
position tells them apart.

Optional because a TICKET settle names its lines by id instead (see
`ticket_line_id`) and the server fills this in — a till settling a ticket
cannot see the order the server will flatten its rounds into, and a
guessed index takes the wrong item off the bill.

ticket_line_id.description:
`open_ticket_items.id` — how a ticket settle names the line to cover.
Resolved to `item_index` by `settle_open_ticket` before pricing.

units.description: How many of that line's units the reward covers. Defaults to one.

allow_negative_balance.description:
When a void or refund claws back points the member has already spent,
may the balance go below zero?

Off (the default) clamps at zero: the shop eats the reward that was
already handed over, and the earn stays visibly part-reversed on the
ledger against an order that says `voided`, so a report can list who
benefited and by how much. On, the balance goes negative and the next
visits earn into the hole — the books balance, and the customer sees a
minus on their card for what was nearly always the shop's own mistake.

Clawbacks ONLY. A redemption or a manual deduction can never overdraw
whatever this says: you cannot spend what you do not have; you can only
owe because a sale you were paid for was undone. Enforced in the
database (`loyalty_apply_txn`), not here.

balance_cap.description:
The ceiling, when `balance_cap_enabled`. `None` = derive it.

A `None` here is NOT "no cap" — that is what the switch is for. It means
the most expensive reward on offer at this scope, read from the
catalogue at award time. Once a customer can claim anything in the
programme, collecting more buys them nothing and leaves the shop
carrying a liability it never chose; and because it is derived, adding a
dearer reward raises the ceiling without anyone retyping it.

Earning at the cap is DROPPED, not refused: the sale is not the
customer's doing and must not fail because their card is full.

balance_cap_enabled.description:
Whether a ceiling applies to what a member may hold at all.

Separate from the figure below, because "no number" has to be able to
mean something. Off, a card collects without end.

birthday_enabled.description:
Ask for a birthday at signup, and greet them on the day.

Off means the form does not ASK — not that it asks and ignores. A date of
birth is the most sensitive thing this feature collects, and a shop that
does not run birthday rewards has no business holding one.

birthday_message.description: Overrides the built-in greeting. `{name}` is substituted; nothing else is.

birthday_reward_amount.description:
Points or stamps given on the day. `None` is a greeting and nothing else,
which is deliberately the default: plenty of shops want to say happy
birthday without giving away a drink.

branch_id.description: `null` = the org-wide default. A branch id = that branch's override.

default_reward_cost.description:
The cost offered by default when an admin adds a reward, in whatever this
scope collects. Each reward may override it, so one catalogue holds
"espresso, 5 visits" beside "cake, 10 visits". Also the pass's fallback
target when no rewards have been curated yet.

earn_include_tax.description: Add tax to the basis. Tips never earn and have no toggle.

earn_on_discounted.description: Earn on what was actually paid rather than the pre-discount subtotal.

earn_piastres_per_point.description:
One point per this many piastres. 1000 = a point per 10 EGP. The
dashboard shows and accepts EGP; the wire is always piastres.

effective_balance_cap.description:
The ceiling actually in force, once derived. **Read-only.**

`balance_cap` is what the shop TYPED, which is usually nothing; this is
what that resolves to against the current catalogue. The dashboard shows
it so "leave it empty" is a visible number rather than a promise, and so
the figure on screen is the one the award path will use rather than the
dashboard's own guess at it.

`null` when no ceiling applies.

enabled.description: The program switch for this scope.

geofenced_branches.description:
How many active branches have coordinates set. **Read-only.**

The one thing that decides whether a saved card can notify a customer
when they are at the shop. Both wallets geofence from the branch
coordinates on the pass, so a programme whose branches have none gets no
location prompt on the phone and no nearby notification — and nothing
anywhere said so, which reads as the wallet being broken rather than as
a field nobody filled in.

Read-only in effect: this type doubles as the PUT body, and the write
path binds its columns explicitly, so a value sent here is parsed and
then ignored. It is a fact about `branches`, answered on this page
because this is where someone wonders why the card is silent.

max_rewards_per_order.description:
How many rewards one order may claim. `None` = unlimited.

`Some(1)` is the setting most shops mean when they ask for this: a
member with thirty stamps and a five-stamp reward can otherwise take six
free items in one visit, which is the same giveaway the shop believed it
was spreading over six.

mode.description:
What this scope collects: `"points"` (from money spent) or `"visits"`
(one stamp per sale). One or the other — never both.

require_otp.description: Verify the signup phone by WhatsApp code, like bookings and ordering.

reward_any_item.description:
Any menu item may be taken as a reward, at `default_reward_cost`.

Off by default. A curated catalogue is the safer shape — it offers an
espresso for five stamps without also offering the steak — and this is
for the shops whose programme genuinely is "collect five, get anything",
which a catalogue can only express by listing the entire menu and
keeping that list in step with it forever.

The two are alternatives, not layers: with this on, the catalogue's
per-item prices no longer apply, because an item's cost can no longer
depend on which item it is.

Defaulted on the way in, because this type is the REQUEST body as well
as the response: every till and dashboard already in the field sends a
settings object without this key, and rejecting those would switch the
programme off for everyone who had not updated yet.

stamp_per_line_item.description:
Count stamps per LINE ITEM rather than per sale. Stamps mode only.

Off, an order of three lattes is one stamp. On, it is three, and a line
of quantity three is three — the rate the customer counts coffees at,
which is what a card saying "buy ten coffees" promised them.

**`None` on the way IN means "leave it as it is."** This type doubles as
the PUT body and a settings save replaces the row wholesale, so a
dashboard built before this field existed would otherwise send `false`
by omission and silently put a per-item programme back on per-order —
or, with the other default, silently triple every existing card's rate.
Neither is a decision a stale browser tab gets to make. A fresh scope
with nothing sent resolves to `true`: that is what a stamp card means,
and a new programme should not need a switch to get it.

Always `Some` on the way OUT; the column is NOT NULL.

winback_enabled.description:
Nudge a member who has not been in for a while. Off by default, like
everything here that speaks to a customer unprompted.

The timing is not a per-shop setting: how long "a while" is, whether it
repeats, and how stale is too stale are one operational judgement across
the estate, and they live in the environment
(`LOYALTY_WINBACK_*`) rather than in a form where a shop could set it to
a day and burn its own list down.

winback_message.description:
ONE override, in whichever language the shop writes it, replacing the
built-in English and Arabic both. `{name}` is substituted; nothing else.

Unset is the better default: the built-ins are written in each language
rather than translated into one, so a customer reads a sentence that was
composed for them.

winback_reward_amount.description: Points or stamps to arrive with the nudge. `None` is words only.

reason.description: Required: a hand-written attendance row always says why it exists.

status.description:
Force a status instead of deriving one — the only way to record an
`absent` or `on_leave` day by hand.

rows_cost_unknown.description: Rows whose cost is unknown under the chosen basis (they ARE in `rows`).

class.description:
Classic menu-engineering class (Kasavana–Smith): `star` | `workhorse` |
`challenge` | `dog`. High/low popularity splits at the 70%-rule
threshold (0.70/n of tracked units); high/low profit splits at the
weighted-average unit contribution margin. `null` for rows that can't
be classified (no sales in the period, or cost unknown).

cost.description: Piastres under the chosen basis; `null` = unknown (never 0).

margin_share_pct.description:
This row's share of the total KNOWN margin (null when margin unknown
or total margin ≤ 0).

on_menu.description:
False when this SKU no longer exists on the active menu (historical
sales under a removed size/item).

popularity_pct.description: This SKU's share of tracked units (the popularity axis), when classified.

prev_quantity.description: Previous equal-length period, for the trend column.

bottom.description: Worst contributors (asc, only rows with known margin), max 3.

top.description: Top contributors by known margin (desc), max 3.

base_cost.description: Piastres per base stock unit, the receipt just before the streak began.

current_cost.description: Piastres per base stock unit, most recent receipt.

streak_length.description:
Number of consecutive received deliveries, most recent first, each
pricier than the one before it.

require_table_for_orders.description:
Every dine-in sale belongs to a table. Re-read on every `/auth/me`, so
switching it on reaches a till that has been running for weeks.

tax_policy.description:
The full policy, including tax-inclusive pricing and service charge.

A till re-reads this whenever it syncs, which is what makes a rate
changed in the dashboard reach a device that has not signed in for
weeks. Without it the till prices under a stale rate and — now that the
server refuses totals it disagrees with — cannot sell at all.

tax_rate.description:
Org tax rate as a decimal (e.g. 0.14 = 14% VAT); 0.0 when the user has no
org. Exposed so the POS can compute a tax-inclusive cart total client-side.

MemberView.description:
A member as the teller, the admin and the pass all see them.

Both balances travel, because an org may switch mode (or run points at one
branch and stamps at another) and what a customer earned under the old rules
is still theirs. `mode` says which one is LIVE where the question was asked,
and `balance` is that one — so a caller never has to pick.

can_redeem.description: The balance affords at least one reward on offer here.

mode.description: `"points"` or `"visits"` — what the branch that asked collects.

next_reward_cost.description:
The cheapest reward on offer here, in `mode`'s currency — what the
progress line counts towards. Falls back to the scope's default cost
when no rewards have been curated.

points_to_next_reward.description:
What that next reward still needs. Equals `next_reward_cost` on an exact
multiple, because a fresh card is the honest thing to show there.

progress_to_next.description:
Progress towards the NEXT reward, after the earned ones are set aside.
`balance % next_reward_cost`.

rewards_ready.description:
How many rewards the balance has ALREADY earned.

A card does not stop at full. Six stamps against a five-stamp reward is
one reward earned and one stamp towards the next, not "five and a bit
wasted" — and a customer who has been in eleven times is owed two
rewards, whether or not they claimed the first.

oneOf.description: Asset refs (Track B4, §11.10); null when no asset or not attached by this endpoint.

all_sizes.description:
Every size row, INCLUDING the synthetic `one_size` one. Additive: this is
where price actually lives, and it is what the dashboard's size editor
and new POS builds read. An item always has at least one entry.

allowed_addon_ids.description: Explicit per-item addon allowlist. Empty = no restriction (use org catalog).

pricing.description:
How a sale line of this item is priced at the requested branch:
madar-catalog's `ItemView` (sizes with their branch prices, the
branch's item price, the recipe's swap bases and their candidates, the
optional fields). The till prices with it exactly as the order path
does. Present on `?full=true` lists; additive, older tills ignore it.

recipe_steps.description:
How the item is made, in order. Each preset step carries its animation's
address and fingerprint, so a device downloads only what its own menu
uses and never the whole library.

sizes.description:
LEGACY SHAPE — unchanged for clients at or below v0.7.11: the synthetic
`one_size` row that now carries a single-price item's price is hidden
here, so an old till still sees a size-less item exactly as it did.

MenuItemWithCosts.description:
A menu item with its per-SKU recipe-cost rollup embedded, so the catalog
list needs no separate `/costing/menu-items` round trip. `sku_costs` is one
row per sellable size (or a single `one_size` row); empty when the item is
inactive or has no recipe.

MethodTotal.description: What the system says one method took on a till.

locale.description: Answer language for translated labels ("en" or "ar").

oneOf.description: Default window for every widget that does not set its own.

timezone.description: The timezone all time buckets were computed in.

ModifierGroupOut.description:
A reusable modifier group attached to this item, with min/max/required resolved
from the attachment overrides (falling back to the group defaults).

ModifierOptionOut.description: A modifier option inside an attached group.

cost_piastres.description: Option recipe cost in piastres (swap markers cost 0). `null` = unknown.

included.description:
`false` = the group offers this option but it is not enabled on this item
(item's `included_option_ids` allowlist excludes it).

table_id.description: The table to move this ticket onto.

MyAttendanceToday.description: What the mobile app shows on its home screen.

blocked_reason.description: Why `can_check_in` is false, in words the app can show verbatim.

branch_id.description:
WHERE to clock in today. Resolved server-side — from the open record, the
rostered shift's branch, or the employee's single branch assignment — so
the app never has to ask. A branch picker would make the geofence
answerable to a dropdown, which defeats the point of having one.
`None` means we cannot tell, and the app should say so rather than guess.

branch_name.description:
That branch's name, so the app's geofence chip can say WHERE it is about
to clock in rather than merely that it can.

business_date.description: The business date in the relevant branch's timezone — not the device's.

oneOf.description: The still-open record, when the employee is currently clocked in.

scheduled.description: Shifts rostered for today. Empty = a rest day.

timezone.description:
The IANA timezone this payload's instants are shown in (see `crate::tz`).
Additive; older clients ignore it.

MyAuthz.description: What the signed-in person may do. The dashboard and POS gate on this.

ask_manager.description: Capabilities not held that show "ask a manager" instead of nothing.

everywhere.description:
The capabilities held at EVERY branch of the business — what an
org-wide act (a department, a shift block, a public holiday, the
rules) needs. `/authz/me` only; absent elsewhere. (E2E B-SETUP-3)

limits.description: Limits on held capabilities, by key; absent = unlimited.

role_kinds.description: Role kinds held here (org_admin, branch_manager, teller, waiter, kitchen).

MyClaim.description:
One of my claims on an open shift, and how it ended (SC-9, S-162): a
request like any other, so it stays in my Requests once decided.

decided_at.description:
When it was decided or withdrawn; null while pending, and on a claim
decided before the server kept this history.

status.description:
`pending` · `approved` · `declined` · `withdrawn`. A shift the
manager took back while the claim waited is `declined`.

my_claims.description:
My claims on open shifts, decided ones included: those on dates in
range, and every pending one wherever it falls (SC-9, S-162).

open_shifts.description: Open shifts at my branches, in published weeks (SC-9).

prefs_set_by.description: `employee` or `manager`: who set my preferences last.

team.description: Colleagues' published shifts at my branches — what a swap can be with.

unpublished_weeks.description: Weeks in range that are not published yet at my branch.

effective_date.description:
The month it lands in (AD-1): any day of that month; the first month
of a recurring line (AD-3). Defaults to today. Must be an open month.

percent_of_base.description: A bonus may be a % of salary.

branch_id.description:
Where it was handed over; defaults to the person's first branch. Must
be a branch the caller may log at.

given_on.description: When the cash changed hands; defaults to today (AV-7).

via.description:
`safe` · `bank`. A till pay-out is tagged on the POS (AV-8), never
logged here by hand (AV-10).

lan_secret.description:
The org's stable LAN-relay secret, hex-encoded. Devices derive a per-branch
HMAC-SHA256 subkey from it to sign every LAN message (Phase E), so only
branch-provisioned devices are trusted on the shared Wi-Fi.

tellers.description:
All PIN-login credentials for the org (tellers, waiters, and kitchen
devices). Field name kept as `tellers` for wire compatibility; it carries
every offline-capable role, distinguished by `role`.

OfflineStamp.description:
What a punch or ping recorded offline carries, so the server can date it
without trusting the phone's wall clock.

anchor.description: The `X-Dawam-Time` value of the last response the phone saw (signed).

elapsed_ms.description: Time-since-boot elapsed from `server_time` to the event, in ms.

gps_time.description:
The GPS fix's own satellite time, when the platform gives one (Android's
GNSS provider; iOS gives none).

rebooted.description: The phone restarted after `server_time`, so `elapsed_ms` means nothing.

server_time.description:
The last server time the phone saw. Only a guide: a valid `anchor`
replaces it, and without one the punch is marked unverified.

offline_pin_hash.description:
argon2id verifier of the user's PIN (derived at online login). `null`
until the user has logged in online at least once.

role.description:
PIN-login role: `teller`, `waiter`, or `kitchen`. The device uses this to
route the offline session (a waiter lands on tickets, a kitchen device on
the KDS) without re-querying the backend.

can_complete.description: True when every `required` step is done (the Finish button enabler).

completed.description:
Derived terminal flag (`completed_at IS NOT NULL`) — the dashboard
routes into the wizard while this is false.

recipe_coverage.description:
Recipe coverage across active menu items (0..1) — drives the cost
engine; surfaced separately because it's a percentage, not a bool.

done.description: True when the underlying data exists.

key.description: Stable key the dashboard switches on — never localized.

required.description:
Steps that are encouraged but not blocking (`required = false`
never gates `can_complete`).

OnlineTaxPolicy.description:
What the storefront needs to render a bill honestly: the rate, and whether
the menu prices already contain it. Sent with the branch list and with every
quote so a page can show a tax line (exclusive) or an "includes VAT" note
(inclusive) instead of quietly under-quoting. No service-charge fields: an
online order never carries one, and a field that is always zero invites a
page to render a line for it.

tax_inclusive.description: `true` = menu prices already contain the tax; the total will not grow.

since.description: `closed_at` of the most recent closed till at the branch.

is_mock.description: The OS's mock-location marker for this fix (CL-9).

oneOf.description:
Set when the cover was queued offline: it starts at its own time, not
when the phone got a signal back (CL-11, audit 03 bug 6).

claimed_at.description: When the live claim was made; null while open.

OpenShiftRequest.description: Request of the legacy open (`till_id` is the removed entity and ignored).

line.description: The frozen priced SnapshotLine (name, size, addons, totals).

round_fired_at.description:
When the round this line came in on was fired. A bill is read as a
sequence of visits to the table — "the drinks at seven, the food at
half past" — and without the clock a till can only show a flat list
that says nothing about how the evening went.

bill.description:
The bill as the SERVER prices it — see [`TicketBill`]. This is the
figure the till shows and the drawer collects, because it is the figure
the settle will book; `subtotal` above is only its first line.

booking_id.description: The booking this ticket seated, if the party had one.

customer_id.description:
The customer this bill belongs to, when one is known (design §2.5): a
table-QR guest who gave a phone, the party's booking, or one the waiter
attached. `customer_name` is the free-text snapshot and may be set
without it. Settling carries it onto the sale.

discount_id.description:
The discount the waiter put on the bill at fire time, if any. Shown so
the cashier can SEE what a settle will inherit — and clear it with an
explicit `discount_type: "none"` rather than have it applied silently.

ready.description:
The kitchen has plated every line of every round. DERIVED from the
ticket's `kitchen_tickets` at read time, so it is always what the KDS
says now. `false` for a ticket nothing was ever fired to the kitchen for
(routing mode `off`): there is nothing to be ready.

ready_at.description:
The last moment the kitchen had the whole ticket plated. History for
the timing reports; `ready` is the live fact.

timezone.description:
The branch's effective IANA timezone (see `crate::tz`) — the zone this
ticket's times are shown in. Additive.

void_reason.description:
Categorised like an order void, so void-rate reports read dine-in and
counter alike.

opening_cash_edited.description:
Ignored. The server decides whether the opening was an edit, from its
own expected carryover — a stale device computes this against a figure
that has since moved on. Kept so older tablets keep parsing.

oneOf.description: Ignored on the live route (live writes `server`).

OptionRecipeLineInput.description:
One recipe line as submitted to the option-recipe replace endpoint. `quantity`
may be 0 (a swap marker). Server normalizes to the ingredient base unit.

size_label.description:
Size this amount is for (`Cup`, `Can`); `null`/absent = every size. At order
time a line for the ordered size's exact label replaces the `null` line for the
same ingredient. Legacy tills only ever see the `null` lines.

customer_id.description:
The customer this sale belongs to (design §2.5) — the same id the sync
feed's order row carries. `customer_name` beside it is the snapshot of
what was typed or printed; this is who it was. A soft reference: `None`
for a walk-in, and it may name a customer since merged (resolve through
`GET /customers/{id}`) or erased.

delivery_channel.description:
Delivery channel ("in_mall" | "outside") of the linked delivery order,
surfaced on the list so clients can flag + segment delivery orders
without a per-order detail fetch. `null` for dine-in orders.

delivery_fee.description:
Delivery charge in piastres, shown separately from the item subtotal.
Always 0 for dine-in orders; for delivery orders
`total_amount == subtotal + tax_amount + delivery_fee` (minus discount).

delivery_lat.description:
Customer location of the linked delivery order, so clients can link out
to a map (e.g. Google Maps) without a per-order detail fetch. `null` for
dine-in orders or delivery orders without captured coordinates.

delivery_order_id.description:
Links a finalized delivery order back to its `delivery_orders` row
(customer, address, channel, zone). `null` for dine-in orders.

device_code.description: That device's code (`36B`), stored with the order. `null` when server-numbered.

device_id.description:
The device that numbered this sale (contract R4). `null` for server-numbered
orders (old clients, dashboard, delivery).

discount_approval_id.description: The manager approval that let the discount past the person's cap. Additive.

discount_approved_by_name.description: The approving manager's name, when the approval was recorded. Additive.

discount_kind.description:
`preset` | `manual_amount` | `manual_percent`; `null` without a
discount or on sales from before discounts were attributed. Additive.

discount_percent_bps.description: The percentage asked for, in basis points. Additive.

discount_rate.description:
The stored value — a fraction for a percentage. Same column as
[`Order::discount_value`].

discount_value.description:
LEGACY SPELLING — an integer, 0-100 for a percentage. See
`discounts::wire`: every shipped till was generated against `integer`,
and a double here fails to deserialise the whole ORDER, not just this
field. Read [`Order::discount_rate`] for the stored number.

display_number.description:
What receipts and lists show: `<device_code>-<order_number>` (`36B-12`)
for a device-numbered sale, else `order_number` as text.

idempotency_key.description:
The client-minted key the sale was created with (a till's sale, or the
ticket id of a settled bill). An offline POS identifies its own row by it
when a list read brings the sale back (OFFLINE_B_DESIGN §7). Additive.

loyalty_customer_id.description: The loyalty member this sale redeemed for (or was scanned for).

loyalty_member_name.description: That member's name, for the order detail. `None` once forgotten.

open_ticket_id.description: The open ticket this sale settled, if any. Additive.

order_ref.description:
Human-readable, org-unique reference (e.g. "DT-260614-0042"). Additive
alongside the per-shift order_number. Optional only during the rollout
window before the historical backfill runs; never null afterwards.

order_type.description:
What kind of sale: "dine_in" (settled from a waiter's ticket — the only
kind that carries a service charge), "takeaway" (rung straight through
the till) or "delivery" (a finalized delivery order). Till sales before
2026-09 say "dine_in" because "takeaway" could not be expressed.

payment_legs.description:
What was ACTUALLY tendered, one entry per `order_payments` row — the same
rows every money report buckets by. A single-tender order has one leg; a
split order has one per leg (e.g. card 285.00 + cash 255.00). Every
response carries them, the one to order creation included.

payment_method.description:
The order's NOMINAL payment label. For a split order this is the literal
`'mixed'` — a label that exists in no money report, because reports bucket
by what was actually tendered. Use [`Order::payment_legs`] for the real
methods; treat this as a display badge only.

price_expected_total.description:
What the catalogue says this sale should have come to, when it differs.
Beside `subtotal` it is the size of the drift, which is the question
anyone looking at a flagged sale asks next.

price_flagged.description:
This sale was rung against a catalogue that has since moved: a line was
charged at a price the menu no longer says, or the item was disabled at
this branch. Both mean a till that was OFFLINE when something changed —
a live sale is priced by the server and cannot deviate.

Recorded, never rejected: the money already changed hands. It is here so
the POS and the dashboard can SHOW it, which is the whole point of
flagging something.

service_charge_amount.description:
The service charge on this bill; `0` where the branch charges none.
Its own field, and its own receipt line: a charge the customer did not
choose is stated separately from the tax rather than folded into it.

service_charge_rate_applied.description:
The service charge rate the bill was priced under (a fraction); `0` on a
takeaway, a delivery, or a bill whose charge was waived. Additive.

service_charge_taxable_applied.description: Whether the service charge sat inside the tax base. Additive.

service_charge_waived_amount.description:
What the removed service charge came to, in minor units; `0` when
nothing was waived. Not part of the total. Additive.

service_charge_waived_at.description: When the service charge was removed. Additive.

service_charge_waived_by.description:
Who removed the service charge from this table's bill (a holder of
`orders:waive_service`), or `null`. Additive.

shift_id.description: DEPRECATED: same value as `till_id` (required by POS v0.5.1/v0.6.0).

started_by.description:
Who started this sale's cart when it is not the person who rang it: a
held order resumed after a teller switch on the till. `null` otherwise.
Additive.

tax_inclusive.description:
Whether this bill's prices included tax, as it was priced. A receipt
says "Prices include VAT" when true. `null` on a read that does not
resolve it. Additive.

tax_rate_applied.description:
The tax rate the bill was priced under (a fraction). `null` for orders
from before rates were recorded. Additive.

timezone.description:
The branch's effective IANA timezone (see `crate::tz`) — the zone every
timestamp on this payload is shown and printed in. Additive: older
clients ignore it; `null` only where a write path does not resolve it.

verification.description:
`server` | `lan` | `unverified` — the till's verification as the ringing
device knew it; `null` when not recorded.

waiter_id.description:
The WAITER who opened this order's ticket (`open_tickets.opened_by`),
stamped server-side at settle time. `null` for direct teller sales and
delivery orders (they never pass through a waiter's ticket).

OrderDeliveryInfo.description:
Customer-facing delivery context attached to a finalized delivery order's
detail view. Sourced from the linked `delivery_orders` row (joined to its
delivery zone for the zone name). The delivery *fee* lives on [Order];
this carries the non-financial fulfilment details a teller/manager needs.

payment_method_hint.description:
Payment method the customer indicated at intake ("cash"/"card"); the
teller confirms the actual method at finalize.

road_distance_meters.description: Road distance (meters) used to price the delivery, when known.

zone_name.description: Name of the matched delivery zone ring, when an outside order matched one.

oneOf.description:
Delivery context (customer phone, address, channel, zone), populated
only on the single-order detail endpoint and only when the order
originated from a delivery order. `null`/absent for dine-in orders.

loyalty_redemption_refused.description:
Set only on the response to a REPLAYED sale whose rewards the points
could not pay for: the covered lines stayed covered, no points moved,
the order is flagged. The till shows this sentence to the teller.

warnings.description:
Non-fatal warnings raised while placing the order — currently used to
flag ingredients that were oversold (stock driven below zero). Empty
for reads/refunds.

items.description: Frozen cart snapshot: the items at the time of the order (for display).

tax_amount.description:
Tax as frozen at intake: inside `total` when `tax_inclusive`, added to
it otherwise.

cost_missing.description: True when any cost component could not be resolved.

is_reward.description:
A loyalty reward paid for some or all of this line. The receipt and the
kitchen say "Reward" beside it.

line_cost.description:
Full line COGS in piastres (recipe + addons + optionals + components).
`null` ⟺ unknown.

reward_covered.description: Minor units the reward took off this line (0 for a paid line).

reward_units.description: How many of `quantity` the reward covered.

staff_comp_minor.description:
A staff drink: what the branch's pool comped on this line, in minor
units, size part and required-choice part together. ALREADY taken off
`line_total` (the size part) and the add-ons' `line_total` (their part):
print it as a line discount, never subtract it again. 0 on a paid line.

unit_cost.description:
Recipe-only cost per unit in piastres (incl. swaps). `null` ⟺ unknown
or bundle line.

line_cost.description:
Ingredient cost of this addon line in piastres. `null` ⟺ unknown, or
a swap addon (its cost lives in the item's recipe cost).

staff_comp_minor.description:
The part of a staff drink's comp this pick absorbed (whole line), already
taken off `line_total`. 0 everywhere else.

oneOf.description:
Put this line on the branch's STAFF POOL: a normal sale whose base
configuration (cheapest size + the default of each required choice) is
comped, extras still charged. Needs `orders.staff_drink.record`. The
server prices the comp; see `docs/staff-drink-comp-contract.md`.
Additive — a client that omits it rings an ordinary paid line. Not
carried by a bundle line (`item_not_eligible`) nor by a ticket's line.

unit_price.description:
What the customer was actually charged, in piastres.

Read ONLY when a queued offline sale is replayed — see [`ClientPrices`].
On the live path the server prices the line and this is ignored, so a
till cannot charge a price of its own choosing and no manual override
exists to let anyone try.

cost.description:
Ingredient cost per parent-item unit in piastres. `null` ⟺ unknown or
no ingredient linked.

stale.description: True when it can no longer be delivered to from the last branch.

OrderNowBranch.description: The branch the customer last ordered from, re-checked now.

channel.description: The channel they last used there.

stale.description:
True when it cannot be used as-is right now; the client falls back to
its branch/channel chooser and keeps the rest of the prefill.

first_name.description: First word of the name on file.

last_branch_name.description: NAME only on the masked path; the full context carries the id.

verify_required.description:
True → this is the masked context; verify the phone
(`/public/otp/request|verify`) and ask again with the device token.

OrderNowFull.description: Everything a verified device gets. Absent from the masked context.

oneOf.description: Derived from the latest order; `None` before the first one.

delivery_fees.description:
Total delivery charges (piastres) across completed orders in scope.
Lets the dashboard surface delivery revenue separately from item sales.

delivery_revenue.description: Gross revenue (total_amount) of completed delivery orders.

in_mall_orders.description: In-mall channel: order count / gross revenue / delivery fees.

line_items.description:
Units sold (SUM of order_items.quantity) across completed orders in
scope. Counts units, not distinct lines, matching the item-sales
reports ("3× burger" contributes 3).

outside_orders.description: Outside channel: order count / gross revenue / delivery fees.

brand_background.description:
The card palette derived from `logo_url` when it was uploaded
(`orgs::branding`). Read-only over the API: there is nothing to set, and
nothing a client may set — the point of deriving is that a shop cannot
choose two colours nobody can read.

brand_card_image.description: A wide photograph for the loyalty card. Own-org editable, like the logo.

brand_logo_is_mark.description:
True when the logo is a shape on transparency, so a card may repaint it
for contrast (`branding::is_mark`). NULL until it has been looked at.

custom_branding.description: The branding tier. Super admin only — see `UpdateOrgRequest`.

modules.description:
Switched-on modules: `pos`, `dawam` (PS-2). Switching one off hides it
and keeps every record.

require_table_for_orders.description:
Every dine-in sale must belong to a table. No effect where a branch has
no floor authored — a shop cannot be made to seat somebody in a room
with no seats.

service_charge_rate.description: Fraction of the bill added as a service charge; `0` disables it.

service_charge_taxable.description: Whether the service charge is itself taxed.

slug.description:
`None` when the shop has no address of its own. Never an empty string —
the column holds NULL for that and a CHECK keeps it so.

social_links.description: Where else to find the shop, keyed by platform. See `orgs::social`.

tax_inclusive.description:
`true` = menu prices already contain the tax, and the receipt breaks it
out backwards rather than adding it on at the till.

tax_rate.description:
Tax rate as a decimal (e.g. `0.14` for 14% VAT).
Stored as `BigDecimal` internally; transmitted as a JSON number.

timezone.description:
IANA timezone name. The org-level default that branches inherit when
their own timezone is unset. Defaults to `Africa/Cairo`.

cost_per_unit.description:
Standard (org default) cost, piastres per unit. `null` ⟺ never entered
(unknown, NOT free) — recipes using this ingredient are cost-missing.

density_g_per_ml.description: Grams per millilitre, bridging weight↔volume in recipes; `null` = none.

pack_size.description: How many BASE STOCK units one `pack_unit` yields; `null` = none.

supplier_id.description: Default supplier for reordering this ingredient; `null` = none set.

stocktake_variance_threshold_pct.description:
Stock-count variance tolerance (percent). A counted row whose |difference|
is at least this percent of book stock is flagged and needs a reason.

OrgModules.description: Which modules an org has switched on.

visible_in_integrations.description:
When false, orders tendered with this method are excluded entirely
from the partner analytics API (`/integrations/analytics/orders`) —
rows and aggregates alike. Defaults to true.

roles.description: Role kinds the template is meant to use.

amount_piastres.description:
The figure to charge instead of the computed one. Zero is allowed — it
means "charge nothing" while keeping the row and its history.

reason.description:
Required. An override with no stated reason is indistinguishable from a
mistake six months later.

units_per_purchase_unit.description:
Stock units per purchase unit. Ignored when `purchase_unit` is a known
inventory unit (the factor is derived from the ingredient's base unit).

match_category_id.description: Menu category (`categories.id`) the rule matches, or `null` = any.

match_item_id.description: One menu item the rule matches, or `null` = any.

match_size_label.description: Exact size label the rule matches (`Cup`, `Can`), or `null` = any.

PaginatedOrdersFull.description:
Same envelope as [PaginatedOrders] but each order carries its line items
(returned when `include_items=true`).

PassLinks.description:
What signup hands the customer. Either side may be absent: a tenant with only
Google credentials configured shows one button, not a broken one.

any.description:
False when neither wallet is configured — the site shows the member's
QR on the page instead of dead buttons.

apple_url.description:
Downloads the signed `.pkpass`. Site-relative, because the signup page
is served from the same origin as the API — so a pass needs a
CERTIFICATE, not a configured base URL.

PastOrder.description: One past visit, as the customer's own page shows it.

items.description:
What they had. The customer asked for this to be here; see the note on
the handler about who else can see it.

total.description: In piastres, like every other figure on the wire.

PatchGroupRequest.description:
Every field optional — only present keys are updated. Nullable columns that must
be clearable (`max_selections`, `swap_category_id`, `legacy_addon_type`) use
presence: key absent = keep, `null` = clear, value = set.

effect.description:
`none` | `adds` | `swaps`. Changing it re-derives `legacy_addon_type` for old
tills: swaps milk → `milk_type`, swaps coffee_bean → `coffee_type`; otherwise
the provided/existing type (a magic type on a non-swap group becomes `extra`).

legacy_addon_type.description: Absent = keep; `null` = clear (group invisible to old tills); a string = set.

max_selections.description: Absent = keep; `null` = no upper bound; a number = set.

swap_category_id.description: Absent = keep; `null` = clear; a category id of this org = set.

replaces_ingredient_id.description: Absent = keep; `null` = clear the swap link; an ingredient id = set.

PatchPackagingRuleRequest.description:
Partial update. A match field is replaced only when its key is present
(`null` clears it); `lines`, when present, replaces the whole set.

is_active.description:
Deactivating a base removes its expanded lines from every size using it
(the pointer stays); reactivating restores them.

advance_cap_piastres.description: The owner's cap on what this person may owe (AV-5), server-computed.

advance_room_piastres.description: How much more can be asked for as an advance (AV-5).

oneOf.description:
So far this period, from the same engine payroll uses (PAY-9). Null
for someone not on payroll.

PaymentLeg.description: One tender against an order (`order_payments`). A split sale has several.

is_cash.description:
The leg's stored cash flag (`order_payments.is_cash`), the one the drawer
counts by. Additive; `null` for a leg recorded before the flag existed.

original_amount_piastres.description:
What the RULE computed, before any human touched it. `None` on a
hand-entered row — nothing was overridden, so there is no "original".

waived_at.description: A waived deduction keeps its amount and stays visible; payroll skips it.

PayrollTotals.description: The whole run's figures, added up by the server (AT-3).

missing_salary_count.description: People on payroll with no salary set (D9); approval waits for them.

carry_out_piastres.description: What deductions exceeded pay by; carried into the next payslip (PAY-12).

paid_method.description:
Paid by `cash` · `bank` · `wallet` (PAY-7), or `none` for a payslip
with nothing to pay, marked by the run itself; null until marked paid.

pay_method.description:
The person's pay method and account at the time of reading, for the
bank and wallet lists (PAY-8).

period_name.description:
The period this covers, denormalised. A payslip identified only by its
generation timestamp is unreadable — two months run on the same day would
be indistinguishable to the employee looking at them.

addons.description: SUM(order_item_addons.quantity) across non-voided orders on this weekday.

avg_orders_per_day.description: Orders averaged over how many times this weekday occurred (may be fractional).

avg_revenue_per_day.description: Revenue in piastres averaged over how many times this weekday occurred in the queried range.

day_of_week.description: Day of week per `EXTRACT(dow ...)`: 0 = Sunday .. 6 = Saturday.

line_items.description: SUM(order_items.quantity) across non-voided orders on this weekday.

orders_pct.description: This weekday's orders as a percentage of the period total (0–100, 1 dp).

revenue_pct.description: This weekday's revenue as a percentage of the period total (0–100, 1 dp).

addons.description: SUM(order_item_addons.quantity) across non-voided orders in this hour bucket.

avg_orders_per_day.description: Orders averaged over the number of calendar days (may be fractional).

avg_revenue_per_day.description: Revenue in piastres averaged over the number of calendar days in the queried range.

line_items.description: SUM(order_items.quantity) across non-voided orders in this hour bucket.

orders_pct.description: This hour's orders as a percentage of the period total (0–100, 1 dp).

revenue_pct.description: This hour's revenue as a percentage of the period total (0–100, 1 dp).

Period.description:
The reporting window.

Prefer a [`PeriodPreset`]: it is resolved server-side against the merchant's
timezone at query time, which means a dashboard widget saying "last 30 days"
stays correct forever, and a language model never has to do calendar
arithmetic — historically the single largest source of wrong answers.

oneOf.description: A named relative window. Takes precedence over `from`/`to`.

PeriodInfo.description:
The resolved window, echoed so a client can label an answer without
re-deriving "last month" itself.

PeriodPreset.description: Named relative windows, resolved in the merchant's timezone.

status.description:
`draft` (reopen an approved month, before anyone is paid) or `closed`
(archive a paid month). Approving is `POST …/generate`; Paid is
reached by marking everyone paid (PAY-7), never by hand.

PermissionMatrix.description:
One cell of the resolved permission matrix for a user.
`effective` = `user_override` if present, else `role_default`, else false.

pin.description: Shown to the admin ONCE. Nothing stores it until it is set on a person.

is_mock.description:
The OS's own mock-location marker (Android `isMock`, iOS
`isSimulatedBySoftware`) (CL-9).

oneOf.description: Set when the ping was queued offline; the server rebuilds its time (CL-11).

charge_phone.description: At 15% or less during a shift: tell them to charge (CL-12).

PointsLiability.description: What the programme owes its members.

currency.description: `"points"` or `"visits"` — the currency the valuation is in.

members_with_balance.description: Live members with a positive balance.

value_per_unit_minor.description:
Minor units one unit of the live currency has bought, on average, over
every redemption this org has recorded (value given ÷ balance spent).
`None` until the first redemption with a recorded value.

valued_minor.description:
The outstanding balance in the live currency × `value_per_unit_minor`,
rounded. An estimate — a balance is worth what it will be spent on.

item_id.description: The menu item or bundle; null for a line with neither.

average_ticket.description: `net_sales / order_count`, rounded half up; 0 with no sales.

net_sales.description: Sold sales net of refunds against them (`branch_sales.total_revenue`).

refunded_orders_count.description: Sales refunded in full (out of every sold figure above).

refunds_issued_count.description: Refunds ISSUED inside the window at this branch, whichever sale they refund.

timezone.description: The IANA zone the days were cut in.

top_items.description: Top [`TOP_ITEMS`] by quantity (then revenue, then name).

window_from.description: `[window_from, window_to)`: local midnight of `from` to local midnight after `to`.

order_count.description: Sold sales with at least one leg in this method.

changed_by_name.description: The manager's name, for a manager's change.

cant_work_days.description: Days I can't work: 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday.

extra_prep_minutes.description:
Minutes the teller adds on top of the branch base prep time. Must be a
non-negative multiple of 5.

PresenceRow.description: One person's state right now, for the manager's live team list.

scheduled_minutes.description:
Minutes this person is rostered for today — the denominator of the
labour-vs-plan bar.

grain.description:
Result shape, so a widget picker knows a KPI card from a line chart
before running anything.

permission.description: Permission resource required, with the `read` action.

cost_missing.description: At least one deducted line has no cost: `total` is partial.

margin_pct.description:
`(price − cost) / price` (fraction, like `/costing`); null when the cost
is partial or the price is 0.

total.description: Piastres over the deducted lines with a known cost.

note.description: `swapped from X` | `follows the chosen X` | `skipped on dine-in`.

price_delta.description: Piastres added to one unit (swap = difference over the default).

base.description: Unit price of the item/size, piastres.

branch_id.description: Price and cost as at this branch; absent = catalogue / org-level cost.

option_ids.description: Chosen modifier options, including item-private optional-field ids.

size_label.description:
Size to price and deduct; absent = the order path's default (base price,
first size's recipe).

defaults.description: Swap groups: group id → the option preselected by the recipe.

size_label.description: The size the preview resolved (the request's, else the default size).

PriceOverrideOut.description: The persisted override row (returned by the upsert).

modules.description:
`pos`, `dawam`; default POS only — Dawam is switched on per org. A
Dawam-only customer is `["dawam"]` (SA-1).

pin.description: Optional six-digit PIN so the owner can also work a till.

today.description: Today's service date in the branch zone (the picker's floor).

device_token.description: From `/public/otp/verify`; required when the branch requires OTP.

PublicBookingView.description: What a guest sees on the manage page — no table ids, no staff fields.

can_modify.description: Still confirmed and further away than the branch's lead time.

in_mall_open_now.description: Effective-open right now (enabled + open shift + override + window).

in_mall_require_location.description: When false, in-mall ordering does not require a device GPS location.

otp_required.description: When false, the public checkout skips OTP verification for this branch.

tax_policy.description:
The tax this branch prices online orders under. The storefront renders
a tax line from it (exclusive) or an "includes VAT" note (inclusive) —
the same policy intake will freeze onto the order.

PublicBrand.description: A shop, as a guest page needs to know it.

background_color.description: `#RRGGBB`. Madar's own when the shop is not on the tier.

custom_branding.description:
Whether the rest of this is the shop's or Madar's.

The page does not need it to render — the palette below is already
resolved — but it decides how loudly Madar signs the footer.

logo_is_mark.description:
True when the logo is a shape on transparency and may be repainted for
contrast. See `orgs::branding::is_mark`.

name.description:
Always the shop's own name, at every tier. A page that does not say
whose it is helps nobody, and that was never the thing being sold.

slug.description:
`None` when the shop has no address of its own — reached by `org_id`,
which every page that already knows the shop uses.

PublicReward.description: A reward as the signup page lists it: what it is, and what it costs.

PublicSocialLink.description:
One place the shop can be found, as a page prints it.

The same three things the wallet passes render (`wallet::apple`,
`wallet::google`), so the card in the phone and the card on the page list
the same links in the same order.

key.description: One of `orgs::social::PLATFORMS` — what the page picks its glyph by.

label.description:
What a human calls it. The page falls back to this where it has no
glyph for `key`, so a platform added on the server still renders.

url.description:
`https://…` and nothing else — checked on write and again on read, see
`orgs::social::links_of`.

PublicTable.description: A table, as the page that opened from its code needs to know it.

accepting.description:
The branch is not serving right now — no till is open. The page says so
instead of letting someone build a basket the kitchen will refuse.

oneOf.description:
The meal in progress, when there is one. `None` means the table is
free and this scan will start the bill.

label.description: What the table is called in the room — "7", "T7", "Terrace 2".

PublicTableBill.description:
What the table has ordered so far.

The page draws this above the menu, so a customer who scans halfway through
a meal sees what is already on their bill rather than an empty basket that
looks like a fresh start. It is also how the second, third and fourth
person at the table see each other's rounds.

Public and unauthenticated, like everything else here. Whoever can read the
code stuck to the table can see what that table ordered — which is the
people sitting at it.

opened_at.description:
When the party's bill was opened. The page counts up from this; a
duration computed here would be wrong by the time it arrived.

ready.description: The kitchen has finished everything fired so far.

rounds.description: Every round fired, oldest first, with what went to the kitchen in each.

subtotal.description: Lines as charged, before discount — the bill's first line, not the bill.

total.description:
What the table will be asked to pay, as the SERVER prices it: the
discount, the service charge and the tax are all in here, and none of
them is something this page should be recomputing.

voided.description:
Taken off the bill after it was ordered — struck through rather than
hidden, so a customer who watches a plate go back sees it go.

week_start.description: Any day of the week; it is rounded to its Saturday.

ledger_page_size.description:
Opt-in paging of a FULL snapshot's ledger rows (tills, orders, cash,
refunds), 100..10000 rows a page. Absent = the whole snapshot in one
response (what every older client gets).

oneOf.description: The `snapshot_cursor` of the previous page of a paged full snapshot.

types.description: Full-fetch ONLY these types (checksum self-heal). Invalid with `since`.

oneOf.description: Full responses only: the latest built base bundle, or null.

Set when the manager's phone queued the punch offline: it is dated at
its own time, not when the phone got a signal back (audit 03 bug 6).

reason.description:
Required (CL-13): a dead phone, a forgotten one. Missing reads as
blank, so the answer is "A reason is required." (Mac E2E BC-4).

branch_name.description:
Branch label — populated by the order lists so the "All branches" view
can show which branch each PO belongs to; other endpoints leave it null.

token.description: The FCM registration token; empty turns pushes off for this phone.

addon_item_ids.description:
Full replacement set of addon item IDs allowed on this menu item.
Send an empty array to clear the restriction (falls back to org catalog).

cover_pay_mode.description:
`minute_rate` · `full_block` (D5). On a branch: its own override;
`inherit: ["cover_pay_mode"]` goes back to the business's.

inherit.description:
Branch only: rules to take from the business again (field names, as
in `overridden`).

needs.description: The whole grid; an empty list clears it.

shifts.description: Every shift the person works that date; empty = a day off.

menu_item_ids.description:
The complete list for this scope, in order. An empty list clears it: for
an org that means every item collects again, for a branch it means going
back to inheriting the org's.

PutEmployeeRequest.description:
Replace an employee's HR profile. Profile fields are a full replace (null
clears them); `name`, `phone`, `app_access` and `branch_ids` are kept when
omitted.

app_access.description: Turning it off signs the phone out.

base_salary_piastres.description:
Piastres. Ignored unless the caller has `hr.payroll.edit` for every
branch — a branch manager editing a job title must not award a raise.

employment_status.description:
`active` | `suspended` | `terminated`. Defaults to `active`. Anything
but `active` signs the phone out (RO-10).

gender.description: `m` · `f`; `null` or empty = not set; omitted keeps what is there.

on_payroll.description:
Paid through Dawam. Like the salary, ignored unless the caller has
`hr.payroll.edit` for every branch.

pay_account.description:
The IBAN or wallet number; `null` or empty clears it; omitted keeps
it. Always cleared when the method is (or stays) `cash`.

pay_method.description:
`cash` · `bank` · `wallet`; omitted keeps what is there. Cash clears
the account.

phone.description: A new number signs the old phone out (RO-10). Empty clears it.

start_time.description: This assignment's own from/to (both or neither).

work_shift_id.description:
Omit (or send null) to mark the date an explicit day off. Otherwise the
whole date becomes this one shift; `PUT /staff/schedules/days` sets a
split day.

steps.description: The whole list, in order. Replaces what was there.

items.description:
The complete list for this scope, in order. An empty list clears the
scope — for a branch that means going back to inheriting the org's.

base_id.description: `null` detaches the size from its base (its base lines are removed).

branch_id.description: Omit for the org default; set for a branch override.

start_time.description: Both, or neither to go back to the block's own times.

QrResponse.description: JSON returned from every QR-generation endpoint.

qr_data_url.description: `data:image/png;base64,…` (or `data:image/svg+xml;base64,…` when `svg=true`). Paste into a browser `` to verify.

branch.description:
Narrow to ONE branch by name. Fuzzy-matched *within* the caller's
accessible branches, so it can only ever narrow, never widen. Dashboards
use the request-level scope instead and leave this unset.

dataset.description: Dataset id — fixes the grain. See `GET /metrics/schema`.

dimensions.description: GROUP BY axes, outermost first. Empty = a single total row.

filters.description: Filter id → chosen value. Each value selects a pre-written predicate.

having_min.description: Only keep groups whose sort measure reaches this value.

measures.description: Aggregates to compute. Empty = the dataset's headline measures.

oneOf.description: Which measure orders the result, and in which direction.

Preferred visualization. Omitted or [`Viz::Auto`] lets the backend pick
from the result shape.

tax_policy.description:
The tax the cart will be priced under at this branch. A quote is a fee
quote — it has no cart, so no tax amount — but the page rendering the
checkout total needs the rate and the inclusivity beside the fee, or it
shows the customer one number and intake records another. Present on
every outcome: the policy is the branch's, not the address's.

unit_cost.description:
Optional ACTUAL invoice cost (piastres per purchase unit) for this
delivery, when it differs from the ordered price. Drives weighted-average
cost + the ledger; omitted ⟹ the PO line's ordered cost is used.

RecipeBaseLineInput.description:
A line as submitted: quantity in `unit`, normalized to the ingredient's base unit
(and grossed up by yield) exactly like a size recipe line.

RecipeBaseLineOut.description: One line of a base, stored in the ingredient's base unit.

quantity.description: Base-unit quantity as a string (numeric fidelity).

size_label.description:
`null` = applies to every size; else only to sizes with this exact label (and
wins over a `null` line for the same ingredient).

item_count.description: Distinct menu items those sizes belong to.

size_count.description: Item sizes currently pointing at this base.

RecipeBaseSaveResult.description: Result of any write that re-expanded recipes.

sizes_changed.description: Sizes (incl. linked copies) whose stored lines changed.

RecipeCostResult.description: Result of a recipe replace: the recomputed size cost.

quantity.description: Submitted quantity (in `unit`); server normalizes to the ingredient base unit.

RecipeLineOut.description: One recipe line, hydrated with the ingredient name and a per-line cost.

line_cost_piastres.description:
Cost of this line in piastres. `null` = UNKNOWN (ingredient unlinked/uncosted),
never shown as 0. A priced line with `quantity = 0` (swap marker) costs 0.

quantity.description: Base-unit, yield-normalized quantity, serialized as a string (numeric fidelity).

size_label.description: Option lines only: the size this amount is for (`null` = every size).

source.description:
Where the line came from: `own` (typed on this size; also legacy NULL rows),
`base` (recipe base), `rule` (packaging rule) or `linked` (copied from the
item this one follows). Only `own` lines are edited by
`PUT /menu-item-sizes/{id}/recipe`.

RecipeLinkInfo.description: Link state of an item, from either side.

in_sync.description:
For a copy: `true` when its stored lines equal the source's for every size label
the copy has (lint F19, twin drift). `null` for an item that is not a copy.

linked_copy_ids.description: Live items whose recipe follows this one.

recipe_source_item_id.description: The item this one's recipe follows, or `null`.

RecipeStep.description:
One step, resolved for display: whatever its kind, it has a name, and a
preset step also carries its note and the animation to play.

animation_hash.description: Content hash of the global asset; `None` until ingested or when retired.

animation_is_global.description: Always true for preset animations (global library).

animation_url.description:
Present only for a preset whose animation still ships. `None` on a
custom step, and on a retired preset — clients show the name alone.

name.description: The preset's name, or the typed name of a custom step.

preset_slug.description: The preset this step uses, if any.

note.description:
What THIS item does at this step ("40ml condensed milk, mixed with the
shot first"). Valid on a preset step too, where it replaces the
library's generic note without giving up the animation.

title.description: The typed name, for `custom`. Either language will do.

RecipeStepPreset.description: One curated step the dashboard offers.

animation_hash.description: Content hash of the zstd-compressed asset (`/assets/global/<hash>.lottie.zst`).

animation_url.description: Path to the animation, relative to the API base.

ReconciliationInput.description: What the teller said about one method at close.

installments.description: 1 = in full from the next payslip (AV-3).

RecordStaffDrinkRequest.description: The body both the live route and the replay op carry.

allowance_at_record.description:
What the DEVICE believed the pool stood at. Kept for the owner to
compare against what the server recomputed; never trusted.

id.description:
Client-minted, and the idempotency key: replaying the same drink twice
is the same row, not a second one off the allowance.

item_name.description: Frozen at the till, so a later rename never rewrites history.

note.description: REQUIRED. Who the drink is for and why, in the teller's own words.

order_id.description: The zero-priced sale this drink rang as, when there is one.

recorded_at.description:
When the teller rang it. Defaults to now; the business day is derived
from this in the BRANCH's timezone, never from the server's clock date.

RecordWasteRequest.description: One waste as a till (or the API) records it.

oneOf.description:
A manager's one-time PIN approval for the LIVE route (owner,
2026-09-17), over the person's `max_value` limit. Additive.

occurred_at.description: When it happened on the device. Default: now.

quantity.description: In `unit`. Whole units for a menu item.

reason.description: expired | spoiled | damaged | overproduction | theft | other

size_label.description: Menu items only: the size whose recipe is wasted (default: the first size).

subject_id.description: An org ingredient id, or a menu item id.

unit.description:
`g` | `kg` | `ml` | `l` | `pcs`. Default: the ingredient's own unit; a
menu item is always `pcs`.

is_cash.description: Whether `method` meant cash when the refund was issued. Snapshotted.

service_charge_amount.description: How much of `amount` was service charge, the same way. Additive.

tax_amount.description:
How much of `amount` was tax, taken back pro rata of the order's own
tax (filled by the database, cumulatively across the order's refunds,
so a full refund takes back exactly the order's tax). Additive.

till_id.description:
The shift the refund was ISSUED in — the drawer the money left. Not
necessarily the till the order was sold in.

order_status.description:
`orders.status` after this refund — `refunded` only when the cumulative
amount reached the total (the trigger's rule, not this module's).

refundable_remaining.description: `total_amount − refunded_amount`: what may still be returned.

RefundIssued.description:
What `POST /refunds` returns: the refund, plus where the order now stands
so the till can print "fully refunded" without a second request.

item_name.description:
`order_items.item_name`, so a receipt reprint names the dish without a
second lookup.

restock.description:
Whether the goods came back. Recorded per line; nothing in this module
writes it `true` yet (see the module docs on restock).

RefundLineInput.description:
One line of the order a refund is for. Optional detail: an overcharge or a
goodwill gesture is an amount with no line behind it.

amount.description:
The share of the refund's amount attributed to this line, minor units.
Zero is allowed (a reward line sent back for nothing). The lines of a
refund may not add up to more than the refund.

quantity.description:
How many of the line's units this refund is for. Held, cumulatively
across every refund of the order, to what the line sold.

RefundReason.description:
Why money went back. The first three share their spelling with
[`crate::orders::VoidReason`] so a report reads "wrong order" across voids
and refunds alike; the rest exist only for refunds (you do not void a sale
for being late). Bound as text; the table's CHECK is the authority on the
vocabulary and this enum mirrors it.

RefundTotals.description:
"Everything returned" — against one order, or in one shift. Read from
`v_order_refund_totals` for an order and summed by `shift_id` for a shift.

refunded_cash.description: The cash slice of `refunded_amount` — what left a drawer.

app.description: Which app this device belongs to, e.g. `"dawam"`.

RegistryInfo.description: The complete registry, as served to a dashboard.

boards.description: Built-in dashboard layouts a merchant can use or fork.

bus.description:
The party ATE here and has paid: the table needs bussing before anyone
else sits, so it lands `dirty` rather than `free`. The same fork the
till makes locally when a parked order checks out versus is discarded --
a discard means nobody ever sat, and the table goes straight back to the
room. Without this the dashboard would show a table with dirty plates on
it as ready for the next party.

ordered_ids.description: Category IDs in the desired display order (first = top).

ReorderLine.description:
One ingredient to reorder, with the quantity needed to reach its order-up-to
level (par_max, else the reorder point).

suggested_qty.description: Quantity (in base units) to bring stock up to the order-up-to level.

ReorderSuggestion.description:
Reorder suggestions grouped by the ingredient's default supplier so the
dashboard can raise one draft PO per supplier.

new_phone_device_token.description: Proof of the NEW phone (the client runs `/public/otp/request|verify` on it).

combined.description: True when two customers were combined into this one.

phone_hint.description: The new number, masked. The client already holds its device token.

ReplayApproval.description:
A manager's approval carried by a queued op (PERMISSIONS_ARCHITECTURE §4.2),
or — the same shape — a live request's one-time manager-PIN unlock (owner,
2026-09-17). `Serialize` + `ToSchema` are for the live half: the offline
queue only ever deserializes one from the wire.

percent_bps.description: Basis points, for an act capped by `max_percent` (a discount). Additive.

value_minor.description: The value an approval covered (`max_value` limits, e.g. a waste).

ReplayFlag.description:
One offline act that was accepted despite failing the permission re-check
(PERMISSIONS_ARCHITECTURE §4.4.5). The money already moved; this is the
owner's notice, not a rollback.

capability.description: The `resource:action` cell the author did not hold.

created_at.description: When it reached us. The gap is the offline window.

occurred_at.description: When the act happened on the device.

reason.description:
`stale_snapshot` — they held it when they acted and the device had not
heard the revocation yet. `unauthorized_offline` — nothing explains it.
`pin_wrong_branch` — their correct PIN was typed at a branch they may
not sign in at (`op` = `PinSignIn`, `details.attempts` counts the tries).

RepricingReport.description: The repricing surface for a branch (or org-wide).

skus_considered.description: Active priced SKUs considered in total.

skus_cost_unknown.description:
Active priced SKUs whose cost is not fully known — NOT suggested (no
guessed cost); surfaced so coverage is transparent.

suggestions.description: Underpriced SKUs with a target-restoring suggestion, biggest uplift first.

RepricingSuggestion.description:
One repricing suggestion: an underpriced SKU + the price that would restore
the target margin.

below_cost.description: True when the item currently sells BELOW cost (negative margin).

suggested_price.description: Target-restoring price `ceil(cost / (1 − target))` to whole EGP, piastres.

target_pct.description: The org/branch target margin this suggestion aims for.

is_paid.description:
Paid or unpaid. REQUIRED when approving leave (RQ-2). For `excuse` and
`early_departure`, omitted falls back to the rule
(`excused_time_paid_default`, branch then business, RQ-7).

note.description:
Required when cancelling someone else's request, or any approved one
(AT-7).

distance_meters.description: Straight-line distance from the supplied coordinates to the branch, in metres.

amount_piastres.description: For `deduct`: the amount the manager typed (CL-7).

reason.description: For `deduct`: why, on the pay line the employee sees (AD-9).

ResolveWarning.description: A resolution problem that the order path only logs; the preview returns it.

rule.description:
`unit_conversion` | `swap_failed` | `optional_not_found` | `optional_size_mismatch`,
or a lint rule id (`F4`…`F10`) when added by the preview.

ResolvedShift.description:
A work shift resolved onto a concrete calendar date, with its window already
converted to UTC instants.

branch_id.description: The branch it is worked at (the block's, else the person's first).

from_override.description: The date holds its own set (a date change), not the pattern.

on_date.description: The business date: the day the shift starts on (SC-10).

scheduled_start_at.description:
The EFFECTIVE window: the assignment's own times, else the block's time
for that weekday, else its default.

start_time.description: Effective wall-clock times in the branch's zone.

times_edited.description: This assignment has its own from/to (shown as edited).

ResultBlock.description:
One dataset the assistant pulled while answering. A turn may carry several —
"compare this month to last" is two.

spec.description:
The exact query that produced this. Sending it back is what makes
