"pin this answer to my dashboard" a single client-side action: the spec
is already a valid widget definition.

title.description: Set when the data came from a curated metric.

quantity.description: Base stock units to return (must be ≤ on hand).

unit_cost.description: Piastres per base stock unit; defaults to the branch's actual cost.

amount_piastres.description: Approve a different amount than asked.

note.description:
Why (kept as the decision note). Required to reject: `note` or
`reason`, `reason` wins (400 `REASON_REQUIRED`, D8).

inherited.description: True when these rows are the org default rather than this branch's own.

base_price.description: Menu price in piastres — what the reward is worth, for the admin's sake.

cost_amount.description:
How much of that currency it costs. Per item, so one catalogue holds
"espresso, 5 visits" beside "cake, 10 visits".

cost_currency.description:
`"points"` or `"visits"` — what this reward is bought with.

Always the currency of the scope this was READ through, never whatever
the row happened to be written with. A program has one mode
([`LoyaltySettings::mode`]) and a reward is priced in it; the stored
column is a record of intent, not an independent fact, and letting the
two disagree is what made a whole catalogue vanish from the till while
the dashboard still listed it.

name.description: Denormalised for display so the teller and the pass need no menu join.

cost_currency.description: `"points"` or `"visits"`. Omitted follows the scope's mode.

editable.description: The owner role holds everything and is not editable.

kind.description: What the role behaves like on older tablets, and its core grants.

prefs_set_by.description: Who set the preferences last: `employee` or `manager` (SC-12).

changed.description: Changed after its week was published (SC-4).

from_override.description: The date holds its own set, not the standing pattern.

on_leave.description: On approved leave or a mission that day.

start_time.description:
Effective wall-clock times at the branch (the assignment's own, else
the block's for that weekday, else its default).

times_edited.description: This assignment has its own from/to (show it as edited).

date_sets.description:
The dates that hold their own set (a date change), a day off included:
the ones "back to the pattern" applies to.

limits_unconfirmed.description: The limits are not yet confirmed by a lawyer; say so beside them.

published_weeks.description: Saturdays of the published weeks in range.

warnings.description:
Labour limits the roster (or, for `overtime_day`, the clock) goes past.
Warnings, never blocks (RU-13).

effective.description: What actually applies right now (auto resolves to kds-if-stations-else-till).

mode.description: Stored override (`kds` | `till` | `both`), or null when auto.

cap_piastres.description:
The owner's cap on what this person may owe in advances, in piastres
(AV-5) — the server's figure, so no client recomputes it. Null for a
caller who may not read this person's salary: the cap is half the
salary, so it would give it away (owner decision D7). The person
always sees their own.

outstanding_piastres.description: What the person owes across their live advances (pending ones count).

within_cap.description:
What is owed (pending ones counted) is within the cap: what a manager
sees instead of the cap (D7). False = over it: only the owner can
approve more.

ScanResult.description: What the teller's scan screen shows.

any_item.description:
The whole menu is claimable, not just `rewards`.

When on, `rewards` stops being the list of what MAY be claimed — it is
only what happens to be curated — and the till offers every line at
`any_item_cost`. Sent rather than inferred, because a till cannot tell
"no catalogue" apart from "any item" without being told.

any_item_cost.description: What one line costs when `any_item` is on, in the branch's currency.

max_rewards_per_order.description:
The shop's ceiling on reward ITEMS per order, if it set one. The till
enforces it before Charge so the server's refusal is never the first
the teller hears of it.

recent.description: Recent history, so a teller can answer "where did my points go?".

rewards.description:
What this member could claim at this branch right now. Empty until the
balance reaches the threshold, so the screen cannot tempt a teller into
handing over a reward that has not been earned.

day_of_week.description:
Postgres `EXTRACT(DOW)` convention: 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday.
`None` = every day of the week.

start_time.description: This assignment's own from/to, when it has one (the block is unchanged).

warnings.description: Labour limits the person's week now goes past. Warnings, never blocks.

ScheduledDay.description: One day of an employee's own upcoming roster.

branch_name.description: The branch each shift is worked at, when the employee has one assignment.

published.description:
The week is published at the person's branch. Unpublished weeks are
drafts: they come back empty (SC-3).

shifts.description: Empty = a rest day, or a week not published yet.

ScopeInfo.description:
Which branches an answer actually covers. Returned on every response so the
scope of a number is never ambiguous — "all branches" versus one of them is
the difference between a figure being right and being off by a factor of
however many branches the merchant has.

all_branches.description: True when the answer spans every branch the caller can access.

label.description: Human-readable label, e.g. "All branches (3)" or "Sidi Henish".

unmatched_branch.description:
Set when a branch was named but could not be matched. The answer then
falls back to the full accessible set, and this flags the mismatch rather
than silently answering a different question.

table_ids.description:
Seat the party on these tables instead (a walk-in took theirs, or the
host prefers another). Omit to keep the claim.

reason.description:
Optional audit note. Never required: an absent or empty reason is
accepted for every capability. Stored (trimmed) when it is sent.

SetParRequest.description: Par levels for one ingredient at one branch. `null` clears a level.

mode.description: `kds` | `till` | `both`, or null to clear the override (back to auto).

customer_id.description: The customer this bill is for; `null` (or absent) takes the customer off.

applied.description: False when nothing was written: unknown customer, unknown or voided bill.

customer_id.description:
What the bill now says, after the merge chain: the survivor of a merged
id, `null` when the customer was taken off, and the PREVIOUS value when
the id was unknown (the pick is dropped, the bill is untouched).

order_id.description:
The sale the change landed on instead, when the bill was already
settled by the time this arrived.

change_given.description:
What the till handed back. Recorded as the drawer saw it, like a
counter sale's; absent, it is derived from `amount_tendered` and the
server's total.

customer_id.description:
The customer this sale belongs to, when the cashier attached one at
settle. Same rules as `customer_id` on an order (needs
`customers.attach`; merged ids resolve; unknown ids are ignored).
Absent, the sale takes the bill's own customer, if it has one.

discount_amount.description:
What the till actually took off this bill, in minor units — the figure
the drawer charged. Additive; absent, the server computes it as before.
This is also what a replayed bill keeps when its preset has since been
switched off: the money as rung, never recomputed from a dead rule.

discount_applied_by.description:
Who put the discount on the bill. Read on replay (live, it is the
cashier holding the token). Additive.

discount_approval_id.description:
The manager approval that let the bill's discount past the cashier's
cap, verified at replay like a counter sale's. Additive.

discount_id.description:
Settle-time discount. ABSENT (all three fields) means the waiter's
ticket discount is inherited, as it always was — but the till can now
see that discount on the ticket view. The literal `discount_type:
"none"` settles with no discount at all; any other value (or a
`discount_id`) replaces the waiter's.

discount_kind.description:
Which discount act this bill performs: `preset` | `manual_amount` |
`manual_percent`. A table bill is gated exactly like a counter sale, so
it names its act in the same vocabulary. ADDITIVE — an older tablet
sends nothing and the kind is derived as it always was (a `discount_id`
means preset, an ad-hoc discount is manual of its type).

discount_percent_bps.description: Basis points for a percentage bill discount (1250 = 12.5%). Additive.

oneOf.description:
A manager's one-time PIN approval for the LIVE settle route (owner,
2026-09-17), same shape and same verification as the replay one.
Additive.

loyalty_customer_id.description: The member spending a balance on this settle, when rewards are applied.

loyalty_redemptions.description:
Rewards covering lines of the ticket. A table-service bill redeems
exactly like a counter one — the cashier scans at settle either way.

payment_splits.description:
Split tenders, when the party paid with more than one. Carried to the
order's payment legs like a counter sale's; they must sum to the total.

settled_at.description:
When the bill was paid, as the till says. An offline settle replayed
later keeps its real time — it becomes the order's `created_at` and the
ticket's `settled_at`, one instant on both rows. Absent means now; a
future clock is refused.

total_amount.description:
What the till says the bill came to — the figure its drawer collected.
Checked against the server's own total exactly as a counter checkout is
(`create_order_inner`'s drift check); a disagreement is refused, not
recorded. Absent on older builds, which then get no check. The figure
to send is `OpenTicketView::bill.total`, which is priced by the same
engine under the same policy — a till that shows that number cannot
disagree with the books.

waive_service_charge.description:
Remove the service charge from this bill. Only someone whose effective
permissions include `orders:waive_service` may send `true`; anyone else
is refused, live or replayed. The order records who and when. Absent
(every build before 0.7.2) means the charge stands.

Shift.description:
Legacy `Shift` = `Till` + `till_id`/`till_name`: the branch's legacy drawer
entity (the one `GET /tills` synthesizes) and its name, exactly as the
pre-rename backend reported them. Build it with [`legacy_shift`].

gross_sales.description:
This shift's sales as rung up, before any refund. Was what
`total_revenue` meant until 2026-09.

refunded_amount.description:
Money refunded AGAINST this shift's sales, whenever and from whichever
drawer it was issued. `gross_sales − refunded_amount = total_revenue`.
A fully refunded sale is out of all three (its status is `refunded`).

refunds_issued_count.description:
Refunds ISSUED IN THIS SHIFT — keyed on `order_refunds.shift_id`, the
drawer the money left, which need not be the shift that made the sale.
This is the Z-report's money-out line: `refunds_issued_cash` is what the
drawer is short by relative to its cash sales.

revenue_by_method.description:
Goods only, by method actually tendered — money IN. Tips are in
`total_tips`; refunds are not netted from these buckets (they are money
OUT, with their own tender — see `refunds_issued_*`).

service_charge_waived_count.description:
Table bills whose service charge was removed by someone holding
`orders:waive_service`, and what those charges came to. Additive.

shift_id.description: DEPRECATED: same value as `till_id` (required by POS v0.5.1/v0.6.0).

total_delivery_fees.description:
Delivery fees on this shift's sales. Inside `total_revenue` (the
customer paid them) but outside the tax base and not food revenue.

total_revenue.description:
What this shift's sales are worth after refunds: `gross_sales` less
`refunded_amount`. Same definition as `total_revenue` on the branch
sales report, so the two reconcile.

total_service_charge.description:
Service charge added to this shift's dine-in bills, less what refunds
took back. Inside `total_revenue` as the shop's income; see
`analytics::schema` for why.

reason.description: The variance reason captured at finalize, or `unexplained` when none.

shrinkage_qty.description: Quantity lost (positive number) from negative stock-count differences.

shrinkage_value.description: Valued shrinkage in piastres; `null` when any contributing cost unknown.

Signal.description:
One advisory flag on a ledger row. `params` carries the evidence numbers the
client templates into a localized reason; `link` names the fix surface.

kind.description:
below_cost | below_target | cost_spike | price_candidate |
removal_candidate | recipe_incomplete

SizeCostOut.description: Live per-size cost of an item from the NEW tables.

cost_piastres.description:
Recipe cost rollup in piastres. `null` = unknown (no priced ingredient),
never 0. A partial rollup returns the sum-so-far with `cost_incomplete=true`.

SizeOut.description: A size (menu_item_sizes row) with its recipe and live cost.

base_id.description: Recipe base this size expands (`PUT /menu-item-sizes/{id}/base`), or `null`.

cost_incomplete.description:
`true` when at least one recipe line is unlinked/uncosted (so `cost_piastres`, if
present, is a partial figure rather than the full COGS).

cost_piastres.description:
Recipe cost rollup in piastres over the priced ingredients. `null` when there is
no recipe or nothing is priced; a partial rollup returns the sum-so-far with
`cost_incomplete = true`.

SizeOverrideOut.description: Per-branch/channel availability & price overrides for a single size.

price.description: Override price in piastres; `null` = inherit the catalog default.

SkuCost.description: Computed cost for one sellable SKU (menu item × size).

cost.description:
Recipe cost rollup in piastres over the ingredients that *are* priced.
`null` only when there is no recipe, or no recipe ingredient has a known
cost at all. A partial rollup (some ingredients unpriced) still returns
the sum so far, with `cost_missing = true` flagging it as incomplete.

cost_missing.description:
`true` when at least one recipe ingredient is unlinked or has no cost, so
`cost` (if any) is a partial figure rather than the full COGS.

food_cost_pct.description: `cost / price` — only when the cost is *complete* and price > 0.

margin_pct.description:
`(price - cost) / price` — only when the cost is *complete* and price > 0.
Suppressed (`null`) for partial rollups so an incomplete cost is never
graded as a food-cost percentage.

price.description: Current price in piastres for this SKU.

size_label.description: `"one_size"` when the item has no sizes.

table_ids.description:
The tables the auto-assigner would pick (host view only; empty when
unavailable).

SnapshotCursor.description:
Where a paged full snapshot stands. Every page reads the same horizon and
window, so the pages together are ONE snapshot: a ledger row that changes
while the pages are fetched moves past the horizon and arrives in the
incremental pull that follows (`since = next`), never twice and never lost.

after_seq.description: Ledger rows with `seq` above this come next.

started_at.description:
When the snapshot began (RFC 3339): a till that closes while the pages
are fetched keeps its rows in the later pages.

window_from.description: The ledger window start of this snapshot (RFC 3339).

SpotViewApproval.description:
A one-time unlock minted on the till: someone holding
`till.cash_spot_check` typed their PIN.

oneOf.description:
Live route: the one-time unlock, when the caller does not hold
`till.cash_spot_check`. (Replay carries it on the envelope.)

approval_id.description: Set by replay from a verified envelope approval (ignored live).

approved_by.description: Set by replay from a verified envelope approval (ignored live).

id.description: Client-minted id; a retry, a replay or the print of the same view is one row.

adjustment_limit_piastres.description: My ceiling on a bonus before it waits for the owner; null = none.

advance_limit_percent.description:
My ceiling on an advance, as whole percent of the person's salary owed
after it (the grant stores basis points); null = none.

caps.description:
The HR capabilities I hold (`hr.*` keys) — through my Madar account;
empty for an employee with none. The app gates tabs on these (PM-4).

caps_everywhere.description:
The capabilities I hold at EVERY branch: the list `GET /authz/me`
puts in `everywhere`, for the business-wide acts (the rules, payroll,
public holidays: `hr.rules.edit`, D3). Empty without a Madar account.

deduction_limit_piastres.description: My ceiling on a deduction (AD-5: separate from the bonus limit).

employee_id.description: Who is signed in: the employee.

modules.description: The org's modules (`pos`, `dawam`); POS on means till punches (CL-13).

privacy_accepted_at.description:
When THIS phone accepted the location notice; null = show it before
any location is taken (AT-5). A new phone, or a restored session on
one that never accepted, starts null.

user_id.description: Their Madar account, when they have one; manager acts go through it.

StaffDrink.description: One recorded staff drink, as every reader sees it.

comp_minor.description:
What the pool comped on the sale's line, minor units, as the SERVER
prices it. `null` on a record-only drink (no priced line behind it).

comp_minor_reported.description:
What the TILL said the comp was, on a replayed sale. Differs from
`comp_minor` exactly when `orders.staff_drink.record:comp_mismatch` was
flagged.

extras_minor.description: What that line was still charged: a bigger size, extras, pricier picks.

overspent.description: Past the allowance, as the SERVER recounted it.

overspent_on_replay.description: The server made it an overspend and the till had not.

StaffDrinkLine.description:
`staff_drink` on an order line. Additive: a client that never heard of it
omits it and the line is an ordinary paid line.

comp_minor.description:
What the TILL comped on this line (whole line, minor units). Read ONLY
when a queued offline sale is replayed; live, the server prices the comp
and this is ignored.

id.description:
Client-minted; the idempotency key AND the `staff_drinks` row's id. A
row an older flow already recorded under this id is reused and the
order attached to it — never a second drink off the allowance.

note.description: REQUIRED. Who the drink is for and why, in the teller's own words.

overspent.description:
Whether the till believed this drink went past the allowance. Replay
only, and only to tell a convergence from a surprise.

StaffDrinksSummary.description: What the staff pool gave away and took in over a range of business days.

comp_minor.description: What the pool comped, minor units (server-priced).

comp_mismatches.description: Rows whose till-reported comp differs from the server's.

cost_minor.description:
What the drinks cost to make, where known. Counts in FULL: the drink
was made whether or not anyone paid for it.

extras_minor.description: What those lines were still charged — the only part that is revenue.

overspent.description: Of those rows, how many went past the allowance.

quantity.description: Drinks (the sum of their quantities) — what the allowance is measured in.

unpriced.description: Record-only rows (no priced sale line behind them; POS ≤ v0.7.12).

key.description: A core i18n key (`staff.n_*`); the app renders it with `args`.

StaffOrgChoice.description: A business the number works at.

active.description: False when the business is suspended: sign-in is stopped (SA-3).

dev_code.description:
The code itself — only from a debug build with `MADAR_DEV_OTP_ECHO=1`,
so a developer can sign in without WhatsApp. Never in release.

org_id.description: The business to sign in to, when the number works at more than one (RO-5).

StaffPoolSettings.description: The settings as the API states them, and as the PUT body accepts them.

branch_id.description: `null` = the org-wide default. A branch id = that branch's override.

daily_allowance.description: Staff drinks this branch may give in one business day.

eligible_item_ids.description: The menu items that count. EMPTY = the pool is off.

enabled.description: The owner's master switch for this scope.

attendance_record_id.description: The record a `correction` proposes to fix. `None` for every other kind.

can_decide.description:
The caller may approve or reject it now: it is pending, not their own,
at one of their branches, and — a manager's request — they outrank
the requester (RQ-5). The same checks the decision makes.

cancelled_by.description: Who cancelled it (the person themselves or a manager), when and why.

cancelled_by_name.description: Who cancelled it, by name, the same way.

decided_by.description:
Who approved or rejected it, when and why. A later cancellation keeps
these (the approval stays on record) and fills `cancelled_*`.

decided_by_name.description:
Who decided it, by name — their employee's name when linked, else
their account's — so a phone that can't look up the owner's account
still names them (RQ-F6).

end_date.description:
Set for `leave` and `mission`: the span's last day. For an `excuse`
that runs past midnight, the next day (its end is then on that day).

from_time.description:
Start of the excused window. `None` = open to the shift's start.
For a `correction`: the proposed check-in, branch-local.

is_own.description: The request is the CALLER's own (worked out for whoever asks).

is_paid.description: Whether the excused time is paid. `None` until decided.

leave_half.description: A half-day leave: `first` or `second` half of the day off (RQ-8).

leave_type_id.description: Deprecated (RQ-2): older rows only; never set on new requests.

month_closed.description:
A day of it is in an approved or paid month: approving or cancelling
approved time is refused (PERIOD_CLOSED); rejecting still works.

paid_default.description:
For a pending excuse or early departure: the business's (or branch's)
rule, which the approve dialog starts from (RQ-7).

record_check_in_at.description:
For a correction: the record's current punches, so an approver sees
what the proposal changes.

to_owner.description:
A manager's own request waiting for someone above them (RQ-5): the
owner decides it. Worked out by the server from capabilities.

to_time.description:
End of the excused window. `None` = open to the shift's end.
For a `correction`: the proposed check-out, branch-local (earlier on the
clock than the check-in = the next morning, a night shift).

work_shift_id.description: The shift a late arrival, early departure or excuse is for (split days).

device_token.description:
Kept in the phone's secure storage and sent as `X-Staff-Device` on
every call (RO-3). It is what refreshes the session.

needs_org.description:
Set when the number works at more than one business and none was
picked: ask, then verify again with `org_id`. The code stays valid.

new_phone.description: True when this sign-in moved the account from another phone.

oneOf.description: The linked account's role; null for an employee with no account.

token.description:
The staff token: `Authorization: Bearer` on `/staff/*` only. It lives
an hour; refresh it with `POST /auth/staff/refresh`.

user_id.description:
Their Madar account when they have one (a manager, a cashier). Manager
acts in the app go through it.

status.description:
Target line step: "confirmed" | "preparing" | "ready" | "out_for_delivery".
The teller may jump to ANY of these from any non-terminal state (forward or
back); the landed step is stamped and all other step stamps are cleared, and
at most one customer WhatsApp fires (the last newly-crossed step that has one).

approved_by_name.description: The manager who approved it on the till.

branch_name.description:
Branch name; only populated by the all-branches waste roll-up (nil
{branch_id}). `None` for single-branch queries that do not select it.

movement_type.description:
inventory_movement_type: sale | void_restock | adjustment_add |
adjustment_remove | waste | transfer_out | transfer_in | purchase_in |
purchase_return | stock_count

occurred_at.description:
When the waste HAPPENED: the device's time for a till waste, the
refund's `issued_at`, the void's `voided_at`, else the post time. The
log is ordered by it.

order_id.description: A refund's or void's waste: the sale.

quantity.description: Signed delta applied to stock (consumption negative, replenishment positive).

received_at.description:
When the server received it (= `created_at`). Differs from
`occurred_at` when a till queued the waste offline.

refund_id.description: A refund's waste: the refund it came from.

unit_cost.description: Piastres per unit at movement time; `null` ⟺ unknown.

waste_quantity.description: The quantity as the person typed it, in `waste_unit`.

waste_source.description:
`pos` | `dashboard` | `refund` (a refunded sale's stock) | `order` (a
made order voided before voids always restocked).

waste_subject_kind.description: `ingredient` | `menu_item`, when the waste was recorded with a header.

waste_subject_name.description: What the person picked (the menu item for an exploded item waste).

waste_value_minor.description: The whole waste's value (all its lines), piastres.

cost_per_unit.description: Piastres per unit; `null` ⟺ cost never entered.

par_min.description: Reorder point; `null` = not set at this branch.

branch_name.description:
Branch label — only populated by the stocktakes list (so the "All
branches" view can show which branch each stocktake belongs to).

counted_items.description: Items counted / items in scope; populated by the list endpoint only.

variance_threshold_pct.description:
Org tolerance: a counted row whose |difference| is >= this percent of
book stock (or that appears-from / vanishes-to zero) is flagged and
requires a `variance_reason` before the count can be finalized.

book_qty.description:
The baseline the difference is measured against: live book stock while
the count is open, frozen at finalize.

is_new.description:
True when the branch had no stock activity for this ingredient when the
count opened — counting it is what starts tracking it here.

opening_qty.description: Book stock when the count was opened (reference only).

variance_reason.description: theft | spoilage | breakage | miscount | supplier_short | transfer_error | other.

reason.description: Why it stops (AD-9). Required: blank or missing is a 400.

specs.description:
The queries that produced the answer — `[{title, preset_id, spec}]`.
Re-running these is how a reopened conversation shows CURRENT figures
rather than the numbers that were true when it was first asked.

StudioAggregate.description: The full item aggregate the one-page Menu Studio editor renders.

oneOf.description: Asset refs (WebP variants, signed), same as `GET /menu-items/{id}`.

linked_copy_ids.description: Live items whose recipe follows this one.

recipe_source_item_id.description: The item this one's recipe follows (linked copy), or `null`.

recipe_steps.description:
How the item is made, in order. Edited through `PUT /recipes/steps/{id}`
and saved by the studio alongside the recipe lines.

co_occurrence_count.description: Number of orders (across the anchor items' order set) this item appeared in.

by_default.description:
The gender default decided it: without it someone else would have
been suggested (it says so).

confidence.description: 0–100. Low (≤ 40) whenever the gender default decided it.

employee_id.description: Who the suggestion puts on the shift.

from_employee_id.description: Who it takes off it, for a reassignment.

id.description: Opaque; send it back to accept or reject.

reason_key.description: A core i18n key for the one-line reason, and its arguments.

start_time.description: The shift's times that day (a day-scoped block's own, else its default).

SyncIngredient.description: An org ingredient referenced by a returned option recipe.

category_id.description:
The ingredient's category (additive, B12), so the POS can mirror the
resolver's "extras follow the drink's choice" pass by slug.

SyncItem.description: One menu item with its sizes and attached modifier groups.

SyncModifierGroup.description:
A modifier group attached to an item, with min/max/required resolved from the
attachment overrides (falling back to the group defaults).

name.description:
The group's authored display name (custom groups have no legacy type —
this is what the POS renders as the section title).

swap_category_id.description: For `swaps`: the ingredient category whose recipe line each option replaces.

SyncOption.description: A modifier option, with price/availability resolved for `(branch, channel)`.

is_default.description:
Explicit preselect for non-swap groups (e.g. "White bread"). Swap groups
derive their default from the drink's recipe; this is always `false` there.

price.description: Effective price in piastres (branch_channel → branch → channel → catalog default).

replaces_ingredient_id.description: The org_ingredient this option swaps out, if it is a swap-style option.

SyncRecipeLine.description:
One recipe line of a modifier option: which ingredient the option deducts
(or swaps in, when `quantity = 0`). Base-unit, yield-normalized values.

quantity.description: Base-unit quantity, serialized as a string for numeric fidelity.

SyncSize.description:
A size (menu_item_sizes row) with its price/availability resolved for the
requested `(branch, channel)`.

price.description: Effective price in piastres (branch_channel → branch → channel → catalog default).

TableBookingHint.description: The slice of a booking the floor needs to show a held/reserved table.

held_from.description: `starts_at - hold_minutes`: from here the table reads as held.

TableHistory.description: What a table has done over the window asked for.

average_bill_minor.description: Mean spend per settled bill, minor units.

average_minutes.description:
Mean minutes a party occupied the table, over settled bills — the
number that says whether a table turns.

sittings.description: Bills opened on this table in the window, newest first.

turns_per_day_x100.description: Settled bills per day over the window, x100 so the wire stays integer.

customer_name.description:
Who is at the table, if they offered a name. Shown on the bill so the
waiter can find them.

customer_phone.description:
Their phone, if they offered one. Optional and never required: with a
valid number (and a name) the bill is linked to that customer — created
on first contact, `source = table_qr` — so the visit counts toward them.
A number that is not valid is ignored; the order is never refused.

idempotency_key.description:
Client-minted, so a phone that resends on a flaky connection does not
order twice. This is the ONLY protection against a double-send, because
a customer's browser has no outbox to dedup against.

items.description: What they want. Named, never priced — see the module docs.

TablePosition.description:
One table's geometry in a bulk drag-save. `section_id` lets a drag move a
table between sections in the same save.

expected_updated_at.description:
Optimistic-concurrency token: the `updated_at` the client last saw for
this table.

The dashboard autosaves every gesture, so two managers arranging the
same room no longer collide rarely and visibly -- they collide often and
silently, each overwriting the other's last drag. When this is sent, the
write only lands if the row has not moved since; otherwise the whole
request is rejected and the caller is told exactly which tables changed.

Optional so existing clients (and the POS) keep working unchanged: absent
means "no guard", which is the previous last-write-wins behaviour.

TableSitting.description: One sitting at a table: the bill that was opened on it and what it came to.

closed_at.description: When the bill was settled or voided; `None` while it is still open.

customer_id.description:
The customer the sitting belongs to, when one is known: the sale's once
settled (a settle may name one the bill never had), else the bill's.
Read through the merge chain, so it is always a live customer.

minutes.description: Minutes from `seated_at` to the close, or to now while still open.

opened_at.description:
When the party's bill was opened — the closest thing the server has to
when they sat down.

order_id.description: The settled sale, when the bill became one.

seated_at.description:
When the party sat down: the seat hold's stamp when they were seated
before ordering, else the bill's opening.

total_amount.description:
What the sale came to, in minor units. `None` for an unsettled or
voided bill — a table's takings only count money that was taken.

TaxPolicyPublic.description:
The tax policy the caller should price under, resolved for their branch
where they have one and their organisation otherwise.

Sent at login and on every `/auth/me`, which is what makes a rate change
reach a till that has been running for weeks. The flat `tax_rate` beside it
is kept for builds that predate this object; both describe the same rate.

service_charge_rate.description: Fraction of the bill added as a service charge; `0` disables it.

service_charge_taxable.description: Whether the service charge is itself taxed.

tax_inclusive.description: `true` = menu prices already contain the tax.

net_revenue.description: `total_amount`, net of refunds, across every branch.

net_tax_due.description: `tax_collected - refunded_tax` — what is actually owed for the period.

org_tax_rate.description:
The org's current tax rate, as a decimal fraction. Informational only —
individual orders carry the rate that was actually applied at sale
time (`tax_rate_applied`), which may differ if the rate changed since.

subtotal.description: Sum of `orders.subtotal` across every branch, before discount or tax.

tax_collected.description:
Tax on every non-voided sale in the range, before refunds (a sale later
refunded in full included).

TeamPresence.description: The whole team's state right now, plus the day's labour against plan.

business_date.description: The branch's business date, in ITS timezone — not the manager's device.

planned_minutes.description: Minutes rostered for today across the team.

timezone.description:
The IANA timezone this payload's instants are shown in (see `crate::tz`).
Additive; older clients ignore it.

worked_minutes.description: Minutes actually worked so far today across the team.

avg_order_value.description: Average bill as rung up — a refund does not shrink what was ordered.

revenue.description: Net of refunds against this teller's sales.

TicketBill.description:
What the party owes, priced where the books are priced.

The till used to show the ticket's running `subtotal` and collect that,
while the settle booked subtotal − discount + service charge + tax. Every
such drawer was short by the tax on every table sale, and the drift check
at settle now refuses that figure outright — so the till must be shown the
right one, and only the server knows the branch's policy. Priced under the
same engine and the same resolved policy as `create_order_inner`, with the
service charge on (a ticket is dine-in by definition, ruling 2). For a
settled ticket the figures are the ORDER's, as booked, not a repricing
under today's policy.

discount_amount.description:
The waiter's discount, resolved (a `discount_id` is looked up the way
the settle looks it up). A cashier who clears it at settle will see a
different total than this one, and that is the point of showing it.

service_charge_taxable.description:
Whether the service charge sits inside the tax base. Frozen on the bill
with the rates, so a till re-pricing the bill (a discount, a reward, a
voided line) prices it the way the settle will. Additive: a bill from
an older server decodes as `true`, `TaxPolicy::default()`'s value.

subtotal.description: Live lines as charged, before discount. Gross when tax-inclusive.

tax_amount.description: Inside the total when `tax_inclusive`, on top of it otherwise.

tax_rate.description: The rates the figures were computed under, for the printed bill.

branch_name.description: Branch label (populated by reads; may be null on some write responses).

held_orders_left_open.description:
Held (parked) orders the closing teller was warned about and left open
for the next till, and their total in minor units. `null` when the
close did not say (older clients, forced closes). Additive.

reconciliation_status.description: `clean` | `disagreed` | `unreviewed` | null (open, or closed before reconciliation existed)

open_at_branch.description:
EVERY open till of the person at THIS branch, newest first (whatever the
device). Normally zero or one; two or more only after an offline open
was replayed while another was open — the newer is flagged
(`opened_while_another_open`) and both stay open, so both are listed.

employee_id.description: The employee the PIN's owner is.

changed_after_close.description: `current_system_total <> system_total` — a late replay moved the total.

shift_id.description: DEPRECATED: same value as `till_id` (POS v0.6.0 decodes `ShiftRefunds`).

TillReportFigures.description:
The report figures shared by the new `TillReportResponse` and the legacy
`ShiftReportResponse` (flattened into both).

refunds_issued_tax.description:
The tax and service charge inside the refunds issued FROM this till's
drawer (`refunds_issued_amount`'s split).

service_charge_waived_count.description:
Table bills whose service charge was removed (`orders:waive_service`),
and what those charges came to. Not part of any total.

spot_views.description: Who viewed (and printed) the cash spot report of this till, oldest first. Additive.

staff_drinks_count.description:
Staff drinks put on the branch's pool during this till, and how many of
them were past the day's allowance. The Z report shows what the shop
gave its own people; the money is zero, so neither figure enters any
total. Additive — an older tablet simply does not read them.

total_service_charge.description: Service charge on this till's sales, less what their refunds took back.

total_tax.description:
Tax on this till's sales, less the tax their refunds took back (a
partial refund takes back its pro-rata share; a voided or fully
refunded sale is out altogether). Additive.

as_of_seq.description:
The branch changefeed horizon read BEFORE the figures (OFFLINE_B_DESIGN
§7): every change with `seq <= as_of_seq` is in this report. A device
whose cursor has reached it, with nothing of the till still on its way,
can take these figures as the authority. `0` when no horizon was
available (then it is never newer than any cursor). Additive.

held_orders_left_open.description: "N held orders left open" at this close (see [`Till`]). Additive.

TillSessionRow.description:
One till session, the way a manager reconciles a drawer: what was in it at
open, what cash the shift put through it, what the teller declared at close,
and what the system says should have been there.

Money is piastres. `null` means *not yet known* (an open till has no closing
figures), never zero — a till still running and a till that counted zero are
different facts.

The cash columns add up: `opening_cash + net_cash_payment + pay_ins −
pay_outs − cash_drops + cash_adjustments` is the drawer's expected cash —
`closing_cash_system` once the till is closed.

branch_code.description: The branch's short code, the prefix of its order references.

business_date.description:
The branch-local calendar day the till was OPENED on — a till opened at
23:50 and closed at 02:10 belongs to the day it opened, which is the
day the takings are reported under.

cash_adjustments.description:
Corrections that name no movement of the three kinds above. Signed:
positive = cash the drawer gained. The till report's `cash_adjustments`.

cash_discrepancy.description: Declared − expected. Negative = short, positive = over.

cash_drops.description:
Cash moved to the safe, net of corrections to safe drops.
Positive = the magnitude that left.

closing_cash_declared.description:
What was counted at close. `null` while the till is open, and for a
force-close nobody counted.

closing_cash_system.description: What the system expected at close. `null` while the till is open.

net_cash_payment.description:
Cash that came in over the counter: cash payments and cash tips on
tendered sales, less cash handed back as refunds from this drawer.

net_sales.description:
Those sales' value, net of what refunds took back (`net_sales` in the
POS metrics report, `revenue` in the teller report).

orders_count.description:
Sales rung on this till, voided and fully-refunded bills excluded —
the same count the teller report uses.

pay_ins.description:
Cash added to the drawer that is not a sale (a float top-up), net of
corrections to pay-ins.

pay_outs.description:
Cash spent out of the drawer, net of corrections to pay-outs.
Positive = the magnitude that left.

TillStatus.description:
OpenAPI-only vocabulary for `Till.status` (the `till_status` DB enum). The
struct fields stay `String`, so the wire strings are exactly the DB values.

TillVerification.description:
OpenAPI-only vocabulary for `Till.verification` (`tills_verification` CHECK):
how the one-open-till-per-person rule was checked when the till opened.
`legacy` marks tills opened by pre-rework clients / before the rework.

addons.description: SUM(order_item_addons.quantity) across non-voided orders in this period.

line_items.description: SUM(order_items.quantity) across non-voided orders in this period.

revenue.description: Net of refunds against the period's sales; `refunded` is what came off.

dimension.description: Which of the chosen dimensions to rank within.

n.description: How many rows to keep per group.

TopReward.description: One reward, by how often it was claimed in the range.

points.description: Balance spent on it, net of anything given back by a void or refund.

redemptions.description: Redemption rows (one per covered order line).

value_minor.description: Minor units of goods given away (what the covered lines were charged).

occupant_kind.description:
Always `open_ticket`. Kept on the wire so the rebuilt booking flow
can queue into the same waitlist without a schema change.

occupant_label.description: Display label for the queue: the held order's name / the ticket's ref.

cumulative.description: Add a running total in time order. Needs a time dimension.

share.description: Add each row's percentage of the grand total.

oneOf.description:
Keep only the top N rows *within* each value of a dimension — "the best
seller in every branch".

force.description: Keep the booking when no table fits after a move (default true).

table_ids.description: Present = reassign to exactly these tables (empty = unassign).

UpdateBranchRequest.description:
PATCH-style update. Fields fall into three categories:

- **Absent** from JSON → keep existing value.
- **Present as `null`** (only the `printer_*` fields) → clear the column.
- **Present as a value** → set to that value.

OpenAPI cannot express the absent-vs-null distinction cleanly, so all
fields are documented as optional and nullable. Clients targeting this
endpoint should send only the fields they want to change.

old_bill_hours.description: Hours after which an open bill counts as old (1..168).

standard_float.description: Standard opening float in minor units (>= 0); explicit `null` clears it.

available_from_time.description:
`null`  → clear the field (no start time restriction)
omitted → keep the existing value
a value → set to that time

unlink_loyalty.description:
DEPRECATED and ignored: leaving the programme is
`DELETE /loyalty/members/{id}`.

custom_branding.description:
May this organisation wear its own mark and colours on the customer's
card and signup page? A paid tier, and this endpoint is already
super-admin only — which is the whole reason it lives here rather than
with the other branding controls an org manager can reach.

logo_url.description:
`null` clears the logo; absent leaves it unchanged. To set a new
logo, use `PUT /orgs/{id}/logo` (multipart) instead — JSON updates
only accept the clear-to-null case here.

modules.description:
`pos`, `dawam`: at least one (PS-2, SA-5). Super admin only, like the
rest of this endpoint.

social_links.description:
Where else to find the shop. Validated against a closed list of
platforms and `https` only — these are printed onto a customer's wallet
pass, and a card that renders whatever was typed can be made to say
anything. See `orgs::social`.

timezone.description:
IANA timezone name (e.g. `Africa/Cairo`). Validated against the
PostgreSQL timezone database. Branches inherit this when their own
timezone is unset.

pin.description:
A NEW PIN is exactly 6 digits; an existing shorter one keeps working
until it is changed.

oneOf.description:
Only org-admins and above can change roles. Promoting to
`super_admin` requires the caller to be a super-admin.

image.description: A wide photograph for the loyalty card. PNG, JPEG or WebP. Required.
Image file (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF still, BMP). Type is sniffed from bytes.

logo.description: Logo image file. PNG, JPEG, or WebP. Required.

UploadResponse.description:
Upload accepted: the picture is converted by the background asset worker.
`image_url` is the row's current legacy URL (unchanged until the job is
done); poll `GET /assets/jobs/{asset_job_id}`.

branch_id.description:
The block's branch; null = the whole business. On an update, omitted
keeps the block's branch (E2E B-ROTA-8); on a create, omitted = the
whole business.

day_times.description:
Its own times on some weekdays (each must be a valid day). Omit to keep
them; an empty list clears them.

ot_day_multiplier.description:
The block's own day-overtime rate (RU-8). Omit to keep it, null to go
back to the branch's rules.

ot_night_multiplier.description: The block's own night-overtime rate. Omit to keep, null to clear.

valid_days.description:
Weekdays it may be rostered on (0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday). Omit to
keep them (all days for a new block).

can_edit.description: Can the caller edit this person's access at all?

locked_reason.description: Why not, when not (self | owner | not_dominant | not_above | missing_authority).

value.description: on_hand × cost_per_unit in piastres; `null` when cost unknown.

net_variance_value.description: overage − shrinkage (net effect on inventory value).

total_shrinkage_value.description: Piastres lost to shrinkage (negative variances), as a positive number.

unknown_cost_count.description: Count of counted rows whose cost was unknown (excluded from totals).

book_qty.description: Book stock the difference is measured against (at finalize).

is_flagged.description: True when |difference| exceeds the org threshold (or appears/vanishes from zero).

opening_qty.description: Book stock when the count opened.

variance_value.description: variance × unit_cost in piastres; `null` when cost unknown.

Viz.description:
How a result is best visualized. A hint: the client may always override, and
[`Viz::Auto`] asks the backend to choose from the [`Grain`].

VoidOpenTicketRequest.description:
Why a bill is torn up. `reason` is typed; `note` is what actually happened,
required when the reason is `other`.

Deserialised leniently, because a void queued offline by an older till
arrives here months later with the picker's LABEL (`"Order mistake"`, or
`"Order mistake — burnt"`) where the enum now is, and a queued op that fails
to parse dead-letters. Those spellings map exactly as migration
`20260912020000` mapped the stored rows; an unrecognised string is `other`
with the whole text as the note, so nothing the waiter wrote is lost.

oneOf.description:
A manager's on-the-spot unlock for a void the teller's own limits do not
allow (someone else's sale, or one older than their window). Additive:
an older till never sends it and is refused exactly as before.

restore_inventory.description:
Ignored: a void always puts the sale's stock back. Kept so older tills
that still send it are read, not refused.

VoidReason.description:
Why a sale or a bill was torn up — the `void_reason` enum, shared by
`orders` and `open_tickets` so a void-rate report reads counter and dine-in
alike without a translation layer. Bound as text and cast in SQL
(`$n::void_reason`), the way the order void has always done it.

WaiterStats.description:
Per-waiter sales split. Only waiter-attributed orders appear (dine-in
settled from a waiter's ticket — `orders.waiter_id IS NOT NULL`); direct
teller sales and delivery orders are out of scope, so totals here are a
subset of the branch overview. `attributed_orders`/`attributed_revenue`
on the report envelope let the UI caption that gap.

avg_items_per_order.description: line_items / orders; 0 when the waiter has no non-voided orders.

avg_order_value.description: Average bill as rung up — a refund does not shrink what was ordered.

line_items.description:
Units sold (SUM of order_items.quantity) on this waiter's non-voided
orders — the upsell signal behind avg_items_per_order.

revenue.description: Net of refunds against this waiter's sales.

WaiterStatsReport.description:
Envelope for the waiters split: rows plus the branch-level totals needed
to caption coverage ("X of Y orders came through waiters").

attributed_orders.description: Non-voided orders in range that carry a waiter.

total_orders.description: All non-voided orders in range (waiter or not).

WalletProvider.description: What a wallet needs before it will offer a button, and whether it has it.

configured.description: Everything present. False means the button is not offered at all.

missing.description: The settings still missing, by name. Empty when `configured`.

reachable.description:
Google only: what Google itself said when asked. `None` for Apple, which
signs locally and has nobody to ask.

apns.description:
Apple's push channel, which is SEPARATE from pass signing.

A pass can be issued perfectly and never change on anyone's phone,
because the two are configured independently — and this panel used to
report Apple as fine while every balance update went nowhere.

WalletStep.description:
One request to Google and what it answered, kept verbatim.

Provisioning is four requests deep and every one of them can fail in a way
the customer never sees: a refused class, an image Google will not fetch, a
field it silently drops. A failed REFRESH is deliberately only a warning —
the customer keeps the card they have — which means the reason lands in a
log nobody is reading at the moment it matters.

So the same code path can be asked to keep a transcript. `save_url` throws
it away; the super-admin diagnostic returns it. One path, so what the
diagnostic reports is what actually happens, rather than a second
implementation that agrees with the first until it doesn't.

body.description: Google's answer, as it came. Truncated only if it is enormous.

status.description: HTTP status, or 0 when the request never reached Google.

step.description: What was attempted, in words: "insert the class", "update the object".

WasteLine.description: One ingredient line of a recorded waste.

quantity.description: Signed ledger delta (negative), in the ingredient's unit.

created.description: `false` when this id had already been recorded (nothing new was posted).

value_minor.description: Piastres at the branch's unit costs; `null` when no line had a cost.

WhatsappStatus.description:
Snapshot returned to the dashboard. Combines the gateway's live link state
with the backend's persisted pause switch.

connected.description: Underlying socket is connected to WhatsApp.

has_qr.description: A pairing QR is currently available to scan.

logged_in.description: A number is linked and ready to send.

paused.description:
Sending is paused by an admin — the number stays linked but every
outbound message (OTP + status) is suppressed until resumed.

qr_image.description: Current pairing QR as a `data:image/png;base64,…` URL (only when `has_qr`).

reachable.description: The gateway answered over HTTP (false = not configured or unreachable).

session.description: Session name the relay pairs/sends under.

WidgetOutcome.description:
A widget either produced a result or an explanation. Never both, never
neither — and a failure here is a 200 with an `error`, not a failed batch.

WidgetRequest.description: One widget in a batch. Exactly one of `preset` or `spec`.

key.description: Caller-chosen key, echoed back so results can be matched to widgets.

oneOf.description: Overrides the batch-level period for this widget alone.
A fully custom query. Same IR the AI agent produces.

branch_id.description: `None` = an org-wide template usable at any branch.

crosses_midnight.description: Derived by the database from `end_time <= start_time`.

day_times.description: Its own times on some weekdays; other valid days use the default.

ot_day_multiplier.description: This block's own day-overtime rate; `None` = the branch's rules (RU-8).

ot_night_multiplier.description: This block's own night-overtime rate; `None` = the branch's rules.

over_presence_cap.description:
Some version of it (default or a weekday's) is longer than the labour
presence cap. A warning, never a block (RU-13).

valid_days.description: The weekdays the block may be rostered on (0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday).

checkin_window_minutes.description:
How long before its start a check-in opens — the window the server
enforces (CL-3), so the app says "opens at" the same time.

day_times.description: Its own times on some weekdays; show that day's times.

valid_days.description:
Weekdays it may be rostered on (0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday): offer it
only on those.

basic_integration.description: Partner analytics credential issued from the dashboard (`POST /integrations/credentials`). Send as `Authorization: Basic base64(username:secret)`. Read-only and scoped to a single branch.

bearer_jwt.description: JWT obtained from `POST /auth/login` (email/password) or `POST /auth/pin-login` (teller PIN). Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
